+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Behaviour — the guilt witness for the cure itself
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+
+class TestSponsorTypeAloneIsNotEvidence:
+    """Re-inject the defect and prove the corpus notices.
+
+    ``_uncured`` removes ONLY the qualifying-fact conjunct from the nine
+    SUPPORT rules, which is exactly the shape PR #6362 shipped for its five.
+    If the census does not move, the qualifying facts are decorative and this
+    whole fold is theatre.
+    """
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def _uncured(seq21_source: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
+        mutated = copy.deepcopy(seq21_source)
+        quals = {row["rule_id"]: row["qualifying_fact"] for row in SUPPORT_RULES}
+        for rule in mutated["rules"]:
+            fact = quals.get(rule["rule_id"])
+            if fact is None:
+                continue
+            rule["when"]["args"] = [
+                arg for arg in rule["when"]["args"] if arg.get("fact") != fact
+            ]
+            rule["required_facts"] = sorted(
+                path for path in rule["required_facts"] if path != fact
+            )
+        return mutated
+
+    def test_stripping_the_qualification_hands_products_out_on_no_evidence(
+        self,
+        seq21_source: dict[str, Any],
+        seq21_compiled: compiler.CompiledRulePack,
+        walks: dict[str, dict[str, Any]],
+    ) -> None:
+        cured = _replay(seq21_compiled, walks)
+        uncured = _replay(_compiled(self._uncured(seq21_source)), walks)
+        moved = [label for label in cured if cured[label] != uncured[label]]
+        assert len(moved) >= 16, (
+            "removing the qualifying facts moved only "
+            f"{len(moved)} walks — the conjuncts are not load-bearing"
+        )
+
+    def test_a_sponsor_type_of_none_would_gain_e33b(
+        self,
+        seq21_source: dict[str, Any],
+        seq21_compiled: compiler.CompiledRulePack,
+        walks: dict[str, dict[str, Any]],
+    ) -> None:
+        """The named guilt: ``offshore/work`` and ``offshore/other`` both
+        declare ``sponsor.type = NONE``. Un-cured, the pack offers them E33B
+        with nothing having established a collaboration."""
+        label = "offshore/work"
+        cured = _decide(seq21_compiled, walks[label]["overrides"], label)
+        uncured = _decide(
+            _compiled(self._uncured(seq21_source)), walks[label]["overrides"], label
+        )
+        assert "E33B" not in cured["candidates"]
+        assert "E33B" in uncured["candidates"]
+
+    def test_a_government_sponsor_would_gain_three_products_at_once(
+        self,
+        seq21_source: dict[str, Any],
+        seq21_compiled: compiler.CompiledRulePack,
+        walks: dict[str, dict[str, Any]],
+    ) -> None:
+        """The dossier's §4 finding, reproduced: un-cured, ONE answer produces
+        E23V + E33A + E33B together because nothing tells them apart."""
+        label = "offshore/work/sponsor_government"
+        cured = _decide(seq21_compiled, walks[label]["overrides"], label)
+        uncured = _decide(
+            _compiled(self._uncured(seq21_source)), walks[label]["overrides"], label
+        )
+        assert cured["candidates"] == ["E23"]
+        assert {"E23V", "E33A", "E33B"} <= set(uncured["candidates"])
+

+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Behaviour — the 84-walk census
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+
+class TestCensusReplay:
+    def test_no_walk_changes_state_or_candidates(
+        self,
+        seq20_compiled: compiler.CompiledRulePack,
+        seq21_compiled: compiler.CompiledRulePack,
+        walks: dict[str, dict[str, Any]],
+    ) -> None:
+        """The honest measurement, and it is a NEGATIVE one: the corpus does
+        not yet carry the ten new facts (W-VO-Q adds the questions), so no walk
+        gains a product. What must NOT happen is a regression — a walk losing
+        its answer, or an ``on_unknown: NEEDS_INPUT`` rule turning a decided
+        dead end into a question."""
+        before = _replay(seq20_compiled, walks)
+        after = _replay(seq21_compiled, walks)
+        drift = [
+            f"{label}: {before[label]['state']} {before[label]['candidates']} -> "
+            f"{after[label]['state']} {after[label]['candidates']}"
+            for label in sorted(before)
+            if (before[label]["state"], before[label]["candidates"])
+            != (after[label]["state"], after[label]["candidates"])
+        ]
+        assert drift == []
+
+    def test_the_census_is_still_67_answers_15_no_paths_2_questions(
+        self,
+        seq21_compiled: compiler.CompiledRulePack,
+        walks: dict[str, dict[str, Any]],
+    ) -> None:
+        census = Counter(actual["state"] for actual in _replay(seq21_compiled, walks).values())
+        assert census["SUPPORTED_CANDIDATES"] == 67
+        assert census["NO_SUPPORTED_PATH"] == 15
+        assert census["NEEDS_INPUT"] == 2
+        assert census["HUMAN_REVIEW_REQUIRED"] == 0
+
+    def test_no_walk_regresses_onto_requested_product_code(
+        self,
+        seq21_compiled: compiler.CompiledRulePack,
+        walks: dict[str, dict[str, Any]],
+    ) -> None:
+        """A4. ``intent.requested_product_code`` is never asked by the browser,
+        so a walk blocked on it is a question the funnel cannot honour."""
+        offenders = [
+            label
+            for label, actual in _replay(seq21_compiled, walks).items()
+            if "intent.requested_product_code" in actual["missing_facts"]
+        ]
+        assert offenders == []
+
+    def test_the_three_generic_dead_ends_now_name_their_cause(
+        self,
+        seq20_compiled: compiler.CompiledRulePack,
+        seq21_compiled: compiler.CompiledRulePack,
+        walks: dict[str, dict[str, Any]],
+    ) -> None:
+        before = _replay(seq20_compiled, walks)
+        after = _replay(seq21_compiled, walks)
+        for label, expected_code in NAMED_CAUSE_WALKS.items():
+            assert before[label]["no_path_reason_codes"] == [_GENERIC_CAUSE], label
+            codes = after[label]["no_path_reason_codes"]
+            assert _GENERIC_CAUSE not in codes, label
+            assert expected_code in codes, label
+            assert after[label]["state"] == "NO_SUPPORTED_PATH", label
+
+    def test_no_other_walk_loses_or_gains_a_no_path_reason(
+        self,
+        seq20_compiled: compiler.CompiledRulePack,
+        seq21_compiled: compiler.CompiledRulePack,
+        walks: dict[str, dict[str, Any]],
+    ) -> None:
+        """INNOCENCE: the two new hard filters touch the three walks they were
+        written for and nothing else."""
+        before = _replay(seq20_compiled, walks)
+        after = _replay(seq21_compiled, walks)
+        moved = sorted(
+            label
+            for label in before
+            if before[label]["no_path_reason_codes"] != after[label]["no_path_reason_codes"]
+        )
+        assert moved == sorted(NAMED_CAUSE_WALKS)
+
+    def test_the_generic_catalogue_sentence_is_gone_from_the_corpus(
+        self,
+        seq21_compiled: compiler.CompiledRulePack,
+        walks: dict[str, dict[str, Any]],
+    ) -> None:
+        offenders = [
+            label
+            for label, actual in _replay(seq21_compiled, walks).items()
+            if _GENERIC_CAUSE in actual["no_path_reason_codes"]
+        ]
+        assert offenders == []

+# FACTS-FOR-THE-TREE — the ten seq-21 qualification facts
+
+> **Audience: W-VO-Q** (the window that adds the interview questions in
+> `apps/mouth/.../_lib/tree.ts`, `flow.ts` and `fact-mapper.ts`).
+> **Pack:** `rulepack-prod-021.source.json`, payload
+> `c21a2aaaa33b939284a8d2ddaedef1f0c22859b3b3a87c9042b48c92814467cf`,
+> `valid_period.from = 2026-09-15T00:00:00Z`. Unsigned, unactivated.
+> **Registry:** `backend/services/visa_engine/enums.py::FactPath` is now 60 paths
+> (56 applicant + 4 derived); every fact below is a `BOOLEAN`, `PiiClass.PERSONAL`,
+> and carries a rollout default of `UNKNOWN / NOT_ASKED` in `models.py`, so an
+> interview that does not yet ask them sends nothing and breaks nothing.
+
+## Why these ten exist, in one paragraph
+
+Nine of the 38 products in the catalogue had **zero** `ELIGIBILITY` rules, which
+makes them structurally unrecommendable: `evaluate_product`'s `declared_coverage`
+is the union of `covered_purposes` over a product's ELIGIBILITY rules, so a
+product with none claims nothing and is feasible for nobody. What each of them
+had instead was a `REQUIRE_REVIEW` rule gated on `intent.requested_product_code`
+— a fact `fact-mapper.ts` hard-codes to `UNKNOWN(NOT_ASKED)`, so the gate was
+dormant and the product invisible. seq-21 retires those nine review rules and
+gives each product one SUPPORT rule keyed on **one qualifying fact**. Until the
+tree asks for that fact, the rule is `on_unknown: NEEDS_INPUT` — the engine asks
+rather than denies. **These ten questions are what turn nine dormant products
+into nine reachable answers.**
+
+## The table
+
+`unlocks` = the product code that becomes a candidate when the fact is `true`
+and the rule's other premises hold. `rule` = the seq-21 rule id that reads it.
+
+| #   | fact id                                     | question (EN)                                                                                                                                                     | question (ID)                                                                                                                                                                        | unlocks                                            | rule                               |
+| --- | ------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------- |
+| 1   | `sponsor.government_invitation`             | Do you hold a written invitation from an Indonesian central-government body, issued to you for your special expertise?                                            | Apakah Anda memiliki undangan tertulis dari instansi pemerintah pusat Indonesia yang diberikan kepada Anda sebagai tenaga ahli?                                                      | **E33A**                                           | `el.e33a.government-invitation`    |
+| 2   | `sponsor.government_collaboration`          | Do you have a confirmed collaboration commitment with an Indonesian government body or institution, based on your special expertise?                              | Apakah Anda memiliki komitmen kolaborasi yang terkonfirmasi dengan instansi atau lembaga pemerintah Indonesia, berdasarkan keahlian khusus Anda?                                     | **E33B**                                           | `el.e33b.government-collaboration` |
+| 3   | `sponsor.world_figure_invitation`           | Has an Indonesian government body invited you as a world figure — a person of international standing?                                                             | Apakah instansi pemerintah Indonesia mengundang Anda sebagai tokoh dunia — seseorang dengan reputasi internasional?                                                                  | **E33C**                                           | `el.e33c.world-figure-invitation`  |
+| 4   | `sponsor.diplomatic_household`              | Is your employer a foreign diplomat posted in Indonesia, and is the role in that diplomat's household?                                                            | Apakah pemberi kerja Anda adalah diplomat asing yang bertugas di Indonesia, dan posisinya berada di rumah tangga diplomat tersebut?                                                  | **E23U**                                           | `el.e23u.diplomatic-household`     |
+| 5   | `sponsor.trade_office`                      | Is your sponsor a foreign trade or economic representative office in Indonesia?                                                                                   | Apakah penjamin Anda adalah kantor perwakilan dagang atau ekonomi asing di Indonesia?                                                                                                | **E23V**                                           | `el.e23v.trade-office`             |
+| 6   | `investment.establishes_indonesian_company` | Will you establish a company in Indonesia as part of this investment?                                                                                             | Apakah Anda akan mendirikan perusahaan di Indonesia sebagai bagian dari investasi ini?                                                                                               | **E28B**                                           | `el.e28b.company-establishment`    |
+| 7   | `investment.capital_market_only`            | Is your investment held only in capital-market instruments, without establishing a company?                                                                       | Apakah investasi Anda hanya ditempatkan pada instrumen pasar modal, tanpa mendirikan perusahaan?                                                                                     | **E28C**                                           | `el.e28c.capital-market`           |
+| 8   | `investment.foreign_branch_or_subsidiary`   | Are you establishing a branch or a subsidiary of a company that already exists outside Indonesia?                                                                 | Apakah Anda mendirikan kantor cabang atau anak perusahaan dari perusahaan yang sudah ada di luar Indonesia?                                                                          | **E28D**                                           | `el.e28d.branch-or-subsidiary`     |
+| 9   | `investment.ikn_subsidiary`                 | Will the company you are establishing be a subsidiary located in the new capital, IKN (Ibu Kota Nusantara)?                                                       | Apakah perusahaan yang Anda dirikan merupakan anak perusahaan yang berlokasi di Ibu Kota Nusantara (IKN)?                                                                            | **E28F**                                           | `el.e28f.ikn-subsidiary`           |
+| 10  | `investment.meets_published_threshold`      | Does your investment meet every published financial minimum for the route you chose — the capital amount, and the annual turnover where that route publishes one? | Apakah investasi Anda memenuhi seluruh batas minimum keuangan yang dipublikasikan untuk jalur yang Anda pilih — jumlah modal, dan omzet tahunan jika jalur tersebut mensyaratkannya? | **E28B · E28C · E28D · E28F** (conjoined with 6–9) | all four `el.e28*` rules           |
+
+## The premises each rule ALSO carries — do not drop them from the branch
+
+A rule only fires when every conjunct is TRUE, and the premises below are the
+ones that make it DEFINITELY FALSE for an applicant the product does not
+concern. They are all facts the tree already asks; the branch that asks a new
+question must keep asking them.
+
+| rule                               | purpose premise                | sponsor / route premise             | qualifying fact |
+| ---------------------------------- | ------------------------------ | ----------------------------------- | --------------- |
+| `el.e23u.diplomatic-household`     | `intent.purposes ⊇ EMPLOYMENT` | `sponsor.type = INDIVIDUAL`         | 4               |
+| `el.e23v.trade-office`             | `intent.purposes ⊇ EMPLOYMENT` | `sponsor.type = GOVERNMENT`         | 5               |
+| `el.e33a.government-invitation`    | `intent.purposes ⊇ EMPLOYMENT` | `sponsor.type = GOVERNMENT`         | 1               |
+| `el.e33b.government-collaboration` | `intent.purposes ⊇ EMPLOYMENT` | `sponsor.type ∈ {GOVERNMENT, NONE}` | 2               |
+| `el.e33c.world-figure-invitation`  | `intent.purposes ⊇ INVESTMENT` | `sponsor.type ∈ {GOVERNMENT, NONE}` | 3               |
+| `el.e28b.company-establishment`    | `intent.purposes ⊇ INVESTMENT` | fact 6 = true                       | 10              |
+| `el.e28c.capital-market`           | `intent.purposes ⊇ INVESTMENT` | fact 7 = true                       | 10              |
+| `el.e28d.branch-or-subsidiary`     | `intent.purposes ⊇ INVESTMENT` | fact 8 = true                       | 10              |
+| `el.e28f.ikn-subsidiary`           | `intent.purposes ⊇ INVESTMENT` | fact 9 = true                       | 10              |
+
+## Where to ask them, and the trap to avoid
+
+- Facts **1–3** belong on the branch that already asks `sponsor_category` and
+  gets `GOVERNMENT` or `NONE`; facts **4–5** on the same question's `INDIVIDUAL`
+  and `GOVERNMENT` answers. Asking all five unconditionally would ask a tourist
+  about a diplomatic household.
+- Facts **6–10** belong on the `invest` branch, after the existing
+  investment-vehicle question. Facts 6–9 are independent booleans on purpose —
+  an applicant establishing a company AND holding capital-market instruments is
+  real, and a single-valued "route" question would force a false choice. Fact 10
+  is asked once, after whichever routes were selected.
+- **`fact-mapper.ts` must map a "no" to `KNOWN false`, not to `unknownFact`.** A
+  false answer makes the rule DEFINITELY FALSE and the product simply not
+  offered; an `unknownFact` leaves the rule UNKNOWN and the engine will ask the
+  question again, which on these `on_unknown: NEEDS_INPUT` rules is a loop.
+- **The rules never appear in `intent.requested_product_code`.** Nothing in
+  seq-21 reads that fact for these nine products (the nine review rules that did
+  are retired), so the tree must not start setting it on their account.
+
+## What proves this file rather than asserts it
+
+`backend/tests/services/visa_engine/test_seq21_pack.py`:
+
+- `TestTheNineProductsAreReachable::test_each_target_product_is_supported_on_its_gold_fixture`
+  builds one fact bag per product from a REAL corpus walk plus the row above,
+  and asserts the engine names the product.
+- `...::test_an_unknown_qualification_asks_instead_of_supporting` withdraws the
+  qualifying fact from each of those nine bags and asserts the product
+  disappears and the outcome becomes `NEEDS_INPUT` — the exact state the
+  interview must cure by asking the question.
+- `TestSponsorTypeAloneIsNotEvidence` strips the qualifying conjunct out of the
+  rules and shows 16 corpus walks then gain products on no evidence: that is the
+  measurement of what these ten facts are load-bearing for.
+
+## Honest limits
+
+- The 84-walk corpus does **not** carry these facts, so the census is unchanged
+  (67 SUPPORTED / 15 NO_SUPPORTED_PATH / 2 NEEDS_INPUT) and the distinct-product
+  count stays 17. Adding the questions is what moves it; the nine gold fixtures
+  above are the proof that the pack side is ready.
+- Each SUPPORT rule declares only the ONE purpose it gates on
+  (`covered_purposes`), not the product's full catalogue coverage. An applicant
+  declaring `{EMPLOYMENT, TOURISM}` therefore still cannot reach E33A, because
+  `COVER_ALL_DECLARED_PURPOSES` needs both covered. Widening that is a pack

   244	        # category, is what this product turns on.
   245	        "premises": [
   246	            {"op": "in", "fact": "sponsor.type", "values": ["GOVERNMENT", "NONE"]},
   247	        ],
   248	        "qualifying_fact": "sponsor.government_collaboration",
   249	        "reason_code": "E33B_GOVERNMENT_COLLABORATION_ELIGIBLE",
   250	    },
   251	    {
   252	        "rule_id": "el.e33c.world-figure-invitation",
   253	        "product_code": "E33C",
   254	        "purposes": ["INVESTMENT"],
   255	        "premises": [
   256	            {"op": "in", "fact": "sponsor.type", "values": ["GOVERNMENT", "NONE"]},
   257	        ],
   258	        "qualifying_fact": "sponsor.world_figure_invitation",
   259	        "reason_code": "E33C_WORLD_FIGURE_INVITATION_ELIGIBLE",
   260	    },
   261	    {
   262	        "rule_id": "el.e28b.company-establishment",
   263	        "product_code": "E28B",
   264	        "purposes": ["INVESTMENT"],
   265	        "premises": [
   266	            {"op": "eq", "fact": "investment.establishes_indonesian_company", "value": True},
   267	        ],
   268	        "qualifying_fact": "investment.meets_published_threshold",
   269	        "reason_code": "E28B_COMPANY_ESTABLISHMENT_ELIGIBLE",
   270	    },
   271	    {
   272	        "rule_id": "el.e28c.capital-market",
   273	        "product_code": "E28C",
   274	        "purposes": ["INVESTMENT"],
   275	        "premises": [
   276	            {"op": "eq", "fact": "investment.capital_market_only", "value": True},
   277	        ],
   278	        "qualifying_fact": "investment.meets_published_threshold",
   279	        "reason_code": "E28C_CAPITAL_MARKET_ELIGIBLE",
   280	    },
   281	    {
   282	        "rule_id": "el.e28d.branch-or-subsidiary",
   283	        "product_code": "E28D",
   284	        "purposes": ["INVESTMENT"],
   285	        "premises": [
   286	            {"op": "eq", "fact": "investment.foreign_branch_or_subsidiary", "value": True},
   287	        ],
   288	        "qualifying_fact": "investment.meets_published_threshold",
   289	        "reason_code": "E28D_BRANCH_OR_SUBSIDIARY_ELIGIBLE",
   290	    },
   291	    {
   292	        "rule_id": "el.e28f.ikn-subsidiary",
   293	        "product_code": "E28F",
   294	        "purposes": ["INVESTMENT"],
   295	        "premises": [
   296	            {"op": "eq", "fact": "investment.ikn_subsidiary", "value": True},
   297	        ],
   298	        "qualifying_fact": "investment.meets_published_threshold",
   299	        "reason_code": "E28F_IKN_SUBSIDIARY_ELIGIBLE",
   300	    },
   301	)
   302	
   303	SUPPORT_RULE_IDS: tuple[str, ...] = tuple(row["rule_id"] for row in SUPPORT_RULES)
   304	
   305	#: Edit 3. The two named-cause hard filters.
   306	E33_GUARANTEE_RULE_ID = "hf.e33.guarantee-below-threshold"
   307	E33_GUARANTEE_REASON = "SECOND_HOME_GUARANTEE_BELOW_THRESHOLD"
   308	#: The two SUPPORT rules whose bounds the EXCLUDE must mirror exactly — read
   309	#: from the pack, never typed here.
   310	E33_DEPOSIT_DONOR_RULE_ID = "el.e33.deposit-basis"
   311	E33_PROPERTY_DONOR_RULE_ID = "el.e33.property-basis"
   312	
   313	EMPLOYMENT_SPONSOR_RULE_ID = "hf.employment-without-indonesian-sponsor"
   314	EMPLOYMENT_SPONSOR_REASON = "PAID_ACTIVITY_WITHOUT_INDONESIAN_SPONSOR"
   315	EMPLOYMENT_SPONSOR_PRODUCT_CODES: tuple[str, ...] = ("E23", "E23V", "E33B")
   316	
   317	HARD_FILTER_RULE_IDS: tuple[str, ...] = (E33_GUARANTEE_RULE_ID, EMPLOYMENT_SPONSOR_RULE_ID)
   318	NEW_RULE_IDS: tuple[str, ...] = SUPPORT_RULE_IDS + HARD_FILTER_RULE_IDS
   319	
   320	#: The nine products this fold makes recommendable.
   321	TARGET_PRODUCT_CODES: tuple[str, ...] = tuple(row["product_code"] for row in SUPPORT_RULES)
   322	
   323	#: The only top-level keys this fold may move; `rules` moves too (retire +
   324	#: insert) but is diffed at the rule level, not by whole-value equality.
   325	_IDENTITY_KEYS = frozenset(
   326	    {
   327	        "sequence",
   328	        "version",
   329	        "rule_pack_id",
   330	        "created_at",
   450	    ``declared_coverage`` is empty". If a base pack has meanwhile given one of
   451	    them a SUPPORT rule, this fold would be adding a SECOND, differently-keyed
   452	    route to the same product without anyone comparing the two; refuse instead.
   453	    """
   454	    for code in TARGET_PRODUCT_CODES:
   455	        existing = _eligibility_rule_ids_for_product(payload, code)
   456	        if existing:
   457	            _fail(
   458	                f"product {code!r} already carries ELIGIBILITY rule(s) "
   459	                f"{sorted(existing)} in the base pack — this fold's premise is "
   460	                "that the nine target products have none, so it refuses rather "
   461	                "than adding a second, unreconciled route to the same product"
   462	            )
   463	
   464	
   465	def _assert_retired_review_rules_are_dormant(payload: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
   466	    """Every rule this fold retires must be a REQUIRE_REVIEW rule gated on
   467	    ``intent.requested_product_code``, scoped to the product it is declared
   468	    against.
   469	
   470	    The retirement's justification is that the rule is dormant BY
   471	    CONSTRUCTION (``fact-mapper.ts`` never sets that fact) and that its review
   472	    question is now a fact the new SUPPORT rule tests. If a future base pack
   473	    gives one of them a condition that can actually fire from the browser,
   474	    retiring it would drop a live gate — so this refuses rather than deleting.
   475	    """
   476	    rules_by_id = _rules_by_id(payload)
   477	    products = _products_by_code(payload)
   478	    for rule_id, product_code in RETIRED_REVIEW_RULES.items():
   479	        rule = rules_by_id.get(rule_id)
   480	        if rule is None:
   481	            _fail(f"rule {rule_id!r} is not in the base pack — the edit set is stale")
   482	        if rule["effect"]["type"] != "REQUIRE_REVIEW":
   483	            _fail(
   484	                f"{rule_id!r} is a {rule['effect']['type']} rule, not REQUIRE_REVIEW — "
   485	                "refusing to retire it under an edit that only claims to retire "
   486	                "dormant review gates"
   487	            )
   488	        if REQUESTED_PRODUCT_FACT not in (rule.get("required_facts") or []):
   489	            _fail(
   490	                f"{rule_id!r} no longer reads {REQUESTED_PRODUCT_FACT} — it can now "
   491	                "fire from the browser, so retiring it would drop a live gate"
   492	            )
   493	        version_id = products[product_code]["product_version_id"]
   494	        if version_id not in rule.get("product_version_ids", []):
   495	            _fail(
   496	                f"{rule_id!r} is not scoped to {product_code} — the declared "
   497	                "rule/product pairing is stale"
   498	            )
   499	
   500	
   501	def _bound_nodes(rule: dict[str, Any], fact: str, op: str) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
   502	    return [
   503	        node for node in _nodes(rule.get("when")) if node.get("fact") == fact and node.get("op") == op
   504	    ]
   505	
   506	
   507	def _e33_guarantee_bounds(payload: dict[str, Any]) -> tuple[int, int]:
   508	    """``(deposit_usd_minimum, property_usd_minimum)``, READ from the two E33
   509	    SUPPORT rules that already encode them.
   510	
   511	    The named-cause EXCLUDE this fold adds says "below the threshold". If the
   512	    number it uses were typed here it could drift from the number the SUPPORT
   513	    rule uses, and the pack would simultaneously deny a product for being
   514	    below X and grant it at Y. Extracting both makes that impossible and turns
   515	    a moved bound into a fold abort.
   516	    """
   517	    rules_by_id = _rules_by_id(payload)
   518	    bounds: list[int] = []
   519	    for rule_id, fact in (
   520	        (E33_DEPOSIT_DONOR_RULE_ID, DEPOSIT_FACT),
   521	        (E33_PROPERTY_DONOR_RULE_ID, PROPERTY_FACT),
   522	    ):
   523	        rule = rules_by_id.get(rule_id)
   524	        if rule is None:
   525	            _fail(f"rule {rule_id!r} is missing — cannot derive the E33 guarantee bound")
   526	        nodes = _bound_nodes(rule, fact, "gte")
   527	        if len(nodes) != 1:
   528	            _fail(
   529	                f"rule {rule_id!r} carries {len(nodes)} '{fact} gte' bounds; exactly "
   530	                "one is required to mirror it unambiguously"
   531	            )
   532	        value = nodes[0]["value"]
   533	        if not isinstance(value, int) or isinstance(value, bool) or value <= 0:
   534	            _fail(f"rule {rule_id!r}'s '{fact} gte' bound is {value!r}, not a positive integer")
   535	        bounds.append(value)
   536	    return bounds[0], bounds[1]
   537	
   538	
   539	def _assert_employment_sponsor_scope_is_coherent(payload: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
   540	    """Every product the employment EXCLUDE is scoped to must declare
   541	    EMPLOYMENT among its ``covered_purposes``.
   542	
   543	    A hard filter conditioned on ``intent.purposes intersects [EMPLOYMENT]``
   544	    that is scoped to a product which cannot cover EMPLOYMENT in the first
   545	    place is dead weight at best and a misleading exclusion reason at worst.
   546	    """
   547	    products = _products_by_code(payload)
   548	    for code in EMPLOYMENT_SPONSOR_PRODUCT_CODES:
   549	        if code not in products:
   550	            _fail(f"product {code!r} is not in the catalogue — cannot scope {EMPLOYMENT_SPONSOR_RULE_ID}")
   551	        covered = products[code].get("covered_purposes") or []
   552	        if "EMPLOYMENT" not in covered:
   553	            _fail(
   554	                f"product {code!r} does not cover EMPLOYMENT ({covered}) — "
   555	                f"{EMPLOYMENT_SPONSOR_RULE_ID} would be scoped to a product its own "
   556	                "condition can never concern"
   557	            )
   558	    if EMPLOYER_IS_INDONESIAN_FACT not in {
   559	        node.get("fact") for rule in payload["rules"] for node in _nodes(rule.get("when"))
   560	    }:
   561	        _fail(
   562	            f"no rule in the base pack reads {EMPLOYER_IS_INDONESIAN_FACT} — the "
   563	            "fact this exclusion turns on is not one the interview establishes, "
   564	            "so the new rule could never fire"
   565	        )
   566

   569	# The edits themselves.

   572	
   573	def build_support_rule(payload: dict[str, Any], row: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
   574	    """One ELIGIBILITY/SUPPORT rule, with its scope, covered purposes and
   575	    citations DERIVED from the product catalogue rather than transcribed."""
   576	    products = _products_by_code(payload)
   577	    code = row["product_code"]
   578	    if code not in products:
   579	        _fail(f"product {code!r} is not in the catalogue — cannot build {row['rule_id']!r}")
   580	    product = products[code]
   581	    purposes = list(row["purposes"])
   582	    unknown = [purpose for purpose in purposes if purpose not in (product.get("covered_purposes") or [])]
   583	    if unknown:
   584	        _fail(
   585	            f"{row['rule_id']!r} would cover {unknown} for {code}, which the product "
   586	            f"catalogue does not list among its covered_purposes "
   587	            f"({product.get('covered_purposes')})"
   588	        )
   589	    when = {
   590	        "op": "all",
   591	        "args": [
   592	            {"op": "intersects", "fact": "intent.purposes", "values": purposes},
   593	            *copy.deepcopy(row["premises"]),
   594	            {"op": "eq", "fact": row["qualifying_fact"], "value": True},
   595	        ],
   596	    }
   597	    return {
   598	        "when": when,
   599	        "scope": "PRODUCTS",
   600	        "stage": "ELIGIBILITY",
   601	        "effect": {
   602	            "type": "SUPPORT",
   603	            "reason_code": row["reason_code"],
   604	            "covered_purposes": purposes,
   605	        },
   606	        "rule_id": row["rule_id"],
   607	        "priority": 100,
   608	        "on_unknown": "NEEDS_INPUT",
   609	        "source_refs": list(product["source_refs"]),
   610	        "valid_period": {"to": None, "from": PACK_VALID_FROM},
   611	        "required_facts": _required_facts(when),
   612	        "explanation_key": f"explain.{row['rule_id']}",
   613	        "safety_critical": False,
   614	        "product_version_ids": [product["product_version_id"]],
   615	    }
   616	
   617	
   618	def build_e33_guarantee_rule(payload: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
   619	    deposit_min, property_min = _e33_guarantee_bounds(payload)
   620	    products = _products_by_code(payload)
   621	    product = products["E33"]
   622	    when = {
   623	        "op": "all",
   624	        "args": [
   625	            {"op": "intersects", "fact": "intent.purposes", "values": ["SECOND_HOME"]},
   626	            {"op": "lt", "fact": DEPOSIT_FACT, "value": deposit_min},
   627	            {"op": "lt", "fact": PROPERTY_FACT, "value": property_min},
   628	        ],
   629	    }
   630	    return {
   631	        "when": when,
   632	        "scope": "PRODUCTS",
   633	        "stage": "HARD_FILTER",
   634	        "effect": {"type": "EXCLUDE", "reason_code": E33_GUARANTEE_REASON},
   635	        "rule_id": E33_GUARANTEE_RULE_ID,
   636	        "priority": 100,
   637	        "on_unknown": "NO_EFFECT",
   638	        "source_refs": list(product["source_refs"]),
   639	        "valid_period": {"to": None, "from": PACK_VALID_FROM},
   640	        "required_facts": _required_facts(when),
   641	        "explanation_key": f"explain.{E33_GUARANTEE_RULE_ID}",
   642	        "safety_critical": False,
   643	        "product_version_ids": [product["product_version_id"]],
   644	    }
   645	
   646	
   647	def build_employment_sponsor_rule(payload: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
   648	    products = _products_by_code(payload)
   649	    when = {
   650	        "op": "all",
   651	        "args": [
   652	            {"op": "intersects", "fact": "intent.purposes", "values": ["EMPLOYMENT"]},
   653	            {"op": "eq", "fact": EMPLOYER_IS_INDONESIAN_FACT, "value": False},
   654	        ],
   655	    }
   656	    source_refs: list[str] = []
   657	    for code in EMPLOYMENT_SPONSOR_PRODUCT_CODES:
   658	        for ref in products[code]["source_refs"]:
   659	            if ref not in source_refs:
   660	                source_refs.append(ref)
   661	    return {
   662	        "when": when,
   663	        "scope": "PRODUCTS",
   664	        "stage": "HARD_FILTER",
   665	        "effect": {"type": "EXCLUDE", "reason_code": EMPLOYMENT_SPONSOR_REASON},
   666	        "rule_id": EMPLOYMENT_SPONSOR_RULE_ID,
   667	        "priority": 100,
   668	        "on_unknown": "NO_EFFECT",
   669	        "source_refs": sorted(source_refs),
   670	        "valid_period": {"to": None, "from": PACK_VALID_FROM},
   671	        "required_facts": _required_facts(when),
   672	        "explanation_key": f"explain.{EMPLOYMENT_SPONSOR_RULE_ID}",
   673	        "safety_critical": False,
   674	        "product_version_ids": [products[code]["product_version_id"] for code in EMPLOYMENT_SPONSOR_PRODUCT_CODES],
   675	    }
   676	
   677	
   678	def build_new_rules(payload: dict[str, Any]) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
   679	    return [
   680	        *(build_support_rule(payload, row) for row in SUPPORT_RULES),
   681	        build_e33_guarantee_rule(payload),
   682	        build_employment_sponsor_rule(payload),
   683	    ]

   686	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   687	# Post-conditions.
   688	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   689	
   690	
   691	def assert_only_expected_changes(before: dict[str, Any], after: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
   692	    """Fail-closed on both axes: name what MAY move and require universal
   693	    equality for everything else, so a key added in some future sequence is
   694	    guarded automatically rather than escaping an allow-list."""
   695	    if set(after) != set(before):
   696	        _fail(
   697	            "the payload's top-level key set changed "
   698	            f"(added {sorted(set(after) - set(before))}, "
   699	            f"removed {sorted(set(before) - set(after))})"
   700	        )
   701	    for key in set(before) - _IDENTITY_KEYS - {"rules"}:
   702	        if _canon(after.get(key)) != _canon(before.get(key)):
   703	            _fail(f"{key} changed — this fold retires and inserts rules and nothing else")
   704	
   705	    before_rules = _rules_by_id(before)
   706	    after_rules = _rules_by_id(after)
   707	
   708	    missing = set(before_rules) - set(after_rules)
   709	    if missing != set(RETIRED_REVIEW_RULES):
   710	        _fail(
   711	            f"removed-rule set mismatch: {sorted(missing)} != "
   712	            f"{sorted(RETIRED_REVIEW_RULES)}"
   713	        )
   714	    added = set(after_rules) - set(before_rules)
   715	    if added != set(NEW_RULE_IDS):
   716	        _fail(f"added-rule set mismatch: {sorted(added)} != {sorted(NEW_RULE_IDS)}")
   717	
   718	    for rule_id, rule in after_rules.items():
   719	        if rule_id in set(NEW_RULE_IDS):
   720	            continue
   721	        if _canon(rule) != _canon(before_rules[rule_id]):
   722	            _fail(
   723	                f"rule {rule_id!r} drifted from seq-20 — this fold edits NO existing "
   724	                "rule, it only retires nine and inserts eleven"
   725	            )
   726	
   727	
   728	def assert_changed_fields_hold_their_expected_values(
   729	    after: dict[str, Any], *, expected_new_rules: list[dict[str, Any]]
   730	) -> None:
   731	    """:func:`assert_only_expected_changes` names what MAY move and excludes it
   732	    from comparison — silent on whether it moved to the RIGHT thing. Pinned
   733	    separately, per the lesson seq-18's review recorded: a guard whose
   734	    fail-closedness holds only while the code above it stays correct is not a
   735	    guard, it is a comment."""
   736	    expected: dict[str, Any] = {
   737	        "sequence": 21,
   738	        "rule_pack_id": str(_rule_pack_id(21)),
   739	        "version": FOLD_VERSION,
   740	        "created_at": FOLD_CREATED_AT,
   741	        "created_by": FOLD_CREATED_BY,
   742	        "valid_period": {"to": None, "from": PACK_VALID_FROM},
   743	        "previous_payload_sha256": SEQ20_PAYLOAD_SHA256,
   744	        "rollback_of_payload_sha256": None,
   745	    }
   746	    for key, want in expected.items():
   747	        got = after.get(key)
   748	        if got != want:
   749	            _fail(f"{key} is {got!r}, expected {want!r}")
   750	
   751	    rules_by_id = _rules_by_id(after)
   752	    for rule_id in RETIRED_REVIEW_RULES:
   753	        if rule_id in rules_by_id:
   754	            _fail(f"rule {rule_id!r} should have been retired but is still present")
   755	
   756	    by_id = {rule["rule_id"]: rule for rule in expected_new_rules}
   757	    for rule_id in NEW_RULE_IDS:
   758	        if _canon(rules_by_id.get(rule_id)) != _canon(by_id[rule_id]):
   759	            _fail(f"{rule_id!r} in the output is not the rule this fold built")
   760	
   761	    # Every target product now has exactly one ELIGIBILITY rule, and it reads
   762	    # that product's own qualifying fact. Stated as an OUTPUT census rather
   763	    # than as nine assertions, so a row added to SUPPORT_RULES without a
   764	    # matching product is caught here too.
   765	    for row in SUPPORT_RULES:
   766	        eligibility = _eligibility_rule_ids_for_product(after, row["product_code"])
   767	        if eligibility != {row["rule_id"]}:
   768	            _fail(
   769	                f"product {row['product_code']!r} ends the fold with ELIGIBILITY "
   770	                f"rules {sorted(eligibility)}, expected exactly [{row['rule_id']!r}]"
   771	            )
   772	        facts = rules_by_id[row["rule_id"]]["required_facts"]
   773	        if row["qualifying_fact"] not in facts:
   774	            _fail(
   775	                f"{row['rule_id']!r} does not read its qualifying fact "
   776	                f"{row['qualifying_fact']!r} — a SUPPORT rule keyed on sponsor "
   777	                "category alone is the exact defect this fold exists to cure"
   778	            )
   779	
   780	
   781	def fold(
   782	    seq20: dict[str, Any],
   783	    seq20_signed: dict[str, Any],
   784	    *,
   785	    observed_at: datetime | None = None,
   786	) -> dict[str, Any]:
   787	    """Return the seq-21 payload, or abort loudly.
   788	
   789	    ``seq20_signed`` is the signed seq-20 envelope and is REQUIRED, not
   790	    optional — see :func:`assert_anchor_is_a_verified_signed_artifact`.
   791	    ``observed_at`` is threaded into that signature check's clock so a test
   792	    pinning it is not left real-clock-dependent.
   793	    """
   794	    digest = hashlib.sha256(canonicalize_json(seq20)).hexdigest()
   795	    if digest != SEQ20_PAYLOAD_SHA256:
   796	        _fail(
   797	            "the seq-20 source is not the activated artifact: recomputed JCS "
   798	            f"digest {digest} != {SEQ20_PAYLOAD_SHA256}. Everything below would "
   799	            "otherwise be built on a payload production never ran."
   800	        )
   801	    assert_anchor_is_a_verified_signed_artifact(seq20_signed, digest, observed_at=observed_at)
   802	    if seq20.get("sequence") != 20:
   803	        _fail(f"expected sequence 20, got {seq20.get('sequence')!r}")
   804	
   805	    inherited_id = seq20.get("rule_pack_id")
   806	    expected_20_id = str(_rule_pack_id(20))
   807	    if inherited_id != expected_20_id:
   808	        _fail(
   809	            f"the seq-20 payload carries rule_pack_id={inherited_id!r}, but the "
   810	            f"uuid5 convention yields {expected_20_id!r} — the anchor is verified, "
   811	            "never assumed."
   812	        )
   813	    collisions = sorted(set(NEW_RULE_IDS) & set(_rules_by_id(seq20)))
   814	    if collisions:
   815	        _fail(f"rule(s) {collisions} already exist in seq-20 — this fold declares them as INSERTs")
   816	
   817	    _assert_target_products_have_no_eligibility_rule(seq20)
   818	    _assert_retired_review_rules_are_dormant(seq20)
   819	    _assert_employment_sponsor_scope_is_coherent(seq20)
   820	
   821	    new_rules = build_new_rules(seq20)
   822	
   823	    out = json.loads(json.dumps(seq20))
   824	    out["rules"] = [rule for rule in out["rules"] if rule["rule_id"] not in RETIRED_REVIEW_RULES]
   825	    out["rules"].extend(copy.deepcopy(rule) for rule in new_rules)
   826	
   827	    out["sequence"] = 21
   828	    out["rule_pack_id"] = str(_rule_pack_id(21))
   829	    out["version"] = FOLD_VERSION
   830	    out["created_at"] = FOLD_CREATED_AT
   831	    out["created_by"] = FOLD_CREATED_BY
   832	    out["valid_period"] = {"to": None, "from": PACK_VALID_FROM}
   833	    out["previous_payload_sha256"] = SEQ20_PAYLOAD_SHA256
   834	    out["rollback_of_payload_sha256"] = None
   835	
   836	    assert_only_expected_changes(seq20, out)
   837	    assert_changed_fields_hold_their_expected_values(out, expected_new_rules=new_rules)
   838	    RulePackPayload.model_validate(out)
   839	    return out
   840

   842	def _assert_output_does_not_collide_with_inputs(output: Path, input_paths: dict[str, Path]) -> None:
   843	    """Refuse to write ``--output`` onto any input path, and refuse an output
   844	    path that merely LOOKS like a signed artifact — verbatim the guard
   845	    ``fold_pack_seq20.py`` carries, for the same reason: a copy-pasted flag
   846	    could otherwise overwrite the SIGNED production anchor with unsigned fold
   847	    bytes."""
   848	    resolved_output = output.resolve()
   849	    for flag, path in input_paths.items():
   850	        if resolved_output == path.resolve():
   250	
   251	#: The engine surface every persisted row and every log line of this module
   252	#: belongs to (migration 252's ``engine_surface`` CHECK admits it verbatim).
   253	_SURFACE = EngineSurface.RECOMMEND
   254	
   255	#: ``visa_engine.enums.VisaPurpose`` (the engine's closed purpose vocabulary,
   256	#: carried by a KNOWN ``intent.purposes`` fact) -> ``request_category``
   257	#: (migration 257's 10-value CHECK). This is the W1 brief Item 3 tile->enum
   258	#: table with the tile step composed away (the v2 interview's tiles bind to
   259	#: these purposes): TOURISM->long_tourism, EMPLOYMENT->work_employee,
   260	#: REMOTE_WORK->work_remote, INVESTMENT->investor,
   261	#: BUSINESS_MEETINGS->business, FAMILY->family, RETIREMENT->retirement,
   262	#: STUDY->student. Purposes with no tile (SECOND_HOME, TRANSIT, MEDICAL,
   263	#: OTHER) deliberately have NO entry — they derive to ``other`` (W1 brief:
   264	#: "unmapped -> other"), never guessed into a neighboring category.
   265	_VISA_PURPOSE_TO_REQUEST_CATEGORY: MappingProxyType[VisaPurpose, str] = MappingProxyType(
   266	    {
   267	        VisaPurpose.TOURISM: "long_tourism",
   268	        VisaPurpose.EMPLOYMENT: "work_employee",
   269	        VisaPurpose.REMOTE_WORK: "work_remote",
   270	        VisaPurpose.INVESTMENT: "investor",
   271	        VisaPurpose.BUSINESS_MEETINGS: "business",
   272	        VisaPurpose.FAMILY: "family",
   273	        VisaPurpose.RETIREMENT: "retirement",
   274	        VisaPurpose.STUDY: "student",
   275	    }

   278	
   279	def resolve_evaluate_mode() -> EngineMode:
   280	    """Resolve the public authority lever; unknown values fail closed to OFF.
   281	
   282	    A per-request canary override (set only by the router, only after the
   283	    canary credential verified — see ``canary_mode_override``) wins over the
   284	    deployment env for the duration of that one request. With no override in
   285	    context this is byte-for-byte the pre-canary behaviour.
   286	    """
   287	
   288	    override = _CANARY_MODE_OVERRIDE.get()
   289	    if override is not None:
   290	        return override
   291	    raw = os.environ.get(EVALUATE_MODE_ENV, EngineMode.OFF.value).strip().upper()
   292	    try:
   293	        return EngineMode(raw)
   294	    except ValueError:
   295	        return EngineMode.OFF
   296	
   297	
   298	def parse_canary_mode(raw: str | None) -> EngineMode | None:
   299	    """The ``EngineMode`` a canary header asks for, or ``None`` if it asks
   300	    for nothing this lever may grant.
   301	
   302	    Closed vocabulary (``SHADOW``/``ENFORCE``, case-insensitive after
   303	    strip). ``None``, empty, ``OFF``, and anything unrecognised all return
   304	    ``None`` — the caller treats that as "not a valid canary request" and
   305	    rejects, rather than silently evaluating under the deployment default.
   306	    """
   307	
   308	    if raw is None:
   309	        return None
   310	    candidate = raw.strip().upper()
   311	    if candidate not in _CANARY_SELECTABLE_MODES:
   312	        return None
   313	    return EngineMode(candidate)
   314	
   315	
   316	def verify_canary_token(presented: str | None) -> bool:
   317	    """Constant-time check of the canary credential.
   318	
   319	    True iff ``CANARY_TOKEN_ENV`` is provisioned (non-empty after strip)
   320	    AND ``presented`` matches it under ``secrets.compare_digest``. Every
   321	    other shape — unset/empty env, missing header, mismatched token, a
   322	    non-ASCII header value — is False. Deliberately a verbatim twin of
   323	    ``verify_driver_token``: same fail-closed posture, same
   324	    re-read-never-cache convention, and a separate secret so holding the
   325	    replay-driver credential does NOT confer the authority to change mode.
   326	    """
   327	
   328	    expected = os.environ.get(CANARY_TOKEN_ENV, "").strip()
   329	    if not expected or not presented:
   330	        return False
   331	    try:
   332	        return secrets.compare_digest(presented, expected)
   333	    except TypeError:
   334	        return False
   335	
   336	
   337	@contextmanager
   338	def canary_mode_override(mode: EngineMode) -> Iterator[None]:
   339	    """Bind ``mode`` as this request's authority, restoring on exit.
   340	
   341	    Restores via the ``ContextVar`` token rather than resetting to ``None``,
   342	    so a nested use cannot silently clear an outer binding.
   343	    """
   344	
   345	    token = _CANARY_MODE_OVERRIDE.set(mode)
   346	    try:
   347	        yield
   348	    finally:
   349	        _CANARY_MODE_OVERRIDE.reset(token)

   352	def resolve_evaluate_shadow_enabled() -> bool:
   353	    """Re-read ``EVALUATE_MODE_ENV`` fresh on every call.
   354	
   355	    True iff the resolved mode is ``SHADOW`` or ``ENFORCE``; anything else
   356	    resolves to ``False``. Authority and persistence semantics are handled by
   357	    :func:`run_evaluation`, which resolves the same lever once per request.
   358	    """
   359	
   360	    return resolve_evaluate_mode() in (EngineMode.SHADOW, EngineMode.ENFORCE)
   361	
   362	
   363	def resolve_response_mode(mode: EngineMode | None = None) -> str:
   364	    """Map the authority lever to the public response contract.
   365	
   366	    SHADOW is comparison-only and therefore CURATED. ENFORCE is authoritative
   367	    and therefore ENGINE, but only after the durable decision write succeeds;
   368	    :func:`run_evaluation` fail-closes a failed ENFORCE write to an ENGINE-mode
   369	    TEMPORARILY_UNAVAILABLE response.
   370	    """
   371	
   372	    resolved = mode or resolve_evaluate_mode()
   373	    return "ENGINE" if resolved is EngineMode.ENFORCE else "CURATED"

   376	def resolve_allowed_synthetic_sources() -> frozenset[str]:
   377	    """The synthetic ``traffic_source`` classes currently allowed from
   378	    callers, parsed fresh from ``ALLOW_SYNTHETIC_SOURCES_ENV`` on every call
   379	    (never cached at import).
   380	
   381	    Comma-separated; each entry is stripped and kept only if it is one of
   382	    migration 256's two synthetic CHECK classes — anything else (including
   383	    ``real``, which needs no allowlist, and arbitrary garbage) is ignored,
   384	    so a malformed env var can never widen the accepted set.
   385	    """
   386	
   387	    raw = os.environ.get(ALLOW_SYNTHETIC_SOURCES_ENV, "")
   388	    return frozenset(
   389	        entry
   390	        for entry in (part.strip() for part in raw.split(","))
   391	        if entry in SYNTHETIC_TRAFFIC_SOURCES
   392	    )

   397	    return raw or _DEFAULT_EVALUATE_ENVIRONMENT

   400	async def _retention_gate_allows_persistence(
   401	    db_pool: asyncpg.Pool,
   402	    *,
   403	    environment: str,
   404	    evaluated_at: datetime,
   405	    request_trace: str,
   406	) -> bool:
   407	    """Fail durable decision processing closed without a Zero policy."""
   408	
   409	    try:
   410	        available = await active_retention_policy_available(
   411	            db_pool,
   412	            environment=environment,
   413	            evaluated_at=evaluated_at,
   414	        )
   415	    except Exception as exc:
   416	        logger.warning(
   417	            "evaluate path: retention policy check failed: %s (trace=%s)",
   418	            type(exc).__name__,
   419	            request_trace,
   420	        )
   421	        return False
   422	    if not available:
   423	        logger.warning(
   424	            "evaluate path: no Zero-approved decision retention policy "
   425	            "for environment=%s (trace=%s)",
   426	            environment,
   427	            request_trace,
   428	        )
   429	    return available

   432	_ReplayPackIdentity: TypeAlias = tuple[uuid.UUID, int, str, str]
   433	
   434	
   435	async def _current_replay_pack_identity(
   436	    db_pool: asyncpg.Pool,
   437	    *,
   438	    environment: str,
   439	    moment: datetime,
   440	) -> _ReplayPackIdentity | None:
   441	    """Resolve and cryptographically verify the authority active *now*."""
   442	
   443	    binding = await _resolve_active_pack_binding(
   444	        db_pool,
   445	        environment=environment,
   446	        effective_at=moment,
   447	        observed_at=moment,
   448	    )
   449	    if binding is None:
   450	        return None
   451	    verified = verify_rule_pack(
   452	        binding.raw_envelope,
   453	        trust_store=StaticTrustStore.from_env(),
   454	        observed_at=moment,
   455	    )
   456	    payload = verified.pack.payload
   457	    if binding.rule_pack_id != payload.rule_pack_id:
   458	        return None
   459	    return (
   460	        payload.rule_pack_id,
   461	        payload.sequence,
   462	        payload.version,
   463	        verified.payload_sha256.hex(),
   464	    )

   466	
   467	async def _replay_authority_matches(
   468	    db_pool: asyncpg.Pool,
   469	    *,
   470	    response: VisaOracleEvaluateResponse,
   471	    expected_environment: str,
   472	    request_trace: str,
   473	) -> tuple[bool, EngineMode]:
   474	    """Double-check mode and active RulePack immediately before replay.
   475	
   476	    Two snapshots make a concurrent activation flip observable. An evaluated
   477	    replay is valid only while its signed RulePack remains the current active
   478	    authority. A TEMP replay has no legal claim, but its response mode must
   479	    still match the live mode.
   480	    """
   481	
   482	    expected_pack: _ReplayPackIdentity | None = None
   483	    if response.decision.state is not DecisionState.TEMPORARILY_UNAVAILABLE:
   484	        rule_pack = response.decision.rule_pack
   485	        if rule_pack is None:  # pragma: no cover - Decision invariant
   486	            return False, resolve_evaluate_mode()
   487	        expected_pack = (
   488	            rule_pack.rule_pack_id,
   489	            rule_pack.sequence,
   490	            rule_pack.version,
   491	            rule_pack.payload_sha256,
   492	        )
   493	
   494	    previous_snapshot: tuple[EngineMode, str, _ReplayPackIdentity | None] | None = None
   495	    for _ in range(2):
   496	        mode = resolve_evaluate_mode()
   497	        environment = _resolve_evaluate_environment()
   498	        moment = datetime.now(timezone.utc)
   499	        if mode is EngineMode.OFF:
   500	            return False, mode
   501	        if environment != expected_environment or response.mode.value != resolve_response_mode(
   502	            mode
   503	        ):
   504	            return False, mode
   505	        if not await _retention_gate_allows_persistence(
   506	            db_pool,
   507	            environment=environment,
   508	            evaluated_at=moment,
   509	            request_trace=request_trace,
   510	        ):
   511	            return False, mode
   512	        try:
   513	            active_pack = (
   514	                None
   515	                if expected_pack is None
   516	                else await _current_replay_pack_identity(
   517	                    db_pool,
   518	                    environment=environment,
   519	                    moment=moment,
   520	                )
   521	            )
   522	        except Exception as exc:
   523	            logger.warning(
   524	                "evaluate path: replay authority check failed: %s (trace=%s)",
   525	                type(exc).__name__,
   526	                request_trace,
   527	            )
   528	            return False, mode
   529	        snapshot = (mode, environment, active_pack)
   530	        if expected_pack is not None and active_pack != expected_pack:
   531	            return False, mode
   532	        if previous_snapshot is not None and snapshot != previous_snapshot:
   533	            return False, mode
   534	        previous_snapshot = snapshot
   535	    return True, previous_snapshot[0]
   536

   568	def derive_request_category(facts: ApplicantFacts, hint: str | None) -> str:
   569	    """The ``request_category`` for this evaluation (migration 257's CHECK).
   570	
   571	    Facts speak first; the hint is honored ONLY when facts derive
   572	    ``other`` (Gemini adversarial pass 2026-07-24, adjudicated MEDIUM — an
   573	    unconditional hint would let any caller relabel a mappable evaluation
   574	    and game the G-a-vol category counts). Resolution order:
   575	
   576	    1. Facts-derived — a KNOWN ``intent.purposes`` fact holding EXACTLY
   577	       ONE purpose maps via ``_VISA_PURPOSE_TO_REQUEST_CATEGORY``. A
   578	       mappable single purpose always wins over any hint.
   579	    2. ``hint`` — the v2 interview's tile, supplied by the caller and
   580	       ALREADY validated against the 10-value enum by the router. Honored
   581	       only in the cases facts cannot express: UNKNOWN purposes,
   582	       multi-purpose facts (no honest primary tile), and purposes with no
   583	       v2 tile (SECOND_HOME/TRANSIT/MEDICAL/OTHER). This is the only path
   584	       that can ever produce ``diaspora``: the engine's closed
   585	       ``VisaPurpose`` vocabulary has no diaspora value (W1 brief Item 3 —
   586	       rejecting the hint would silently miscount diaspora demand as
   587	       ``other``, the exact outcome Fable rejected).
   588	    3. ``other`` — the floor, never guessed.
   589	    """
   590	
   591	    derived = "other"
   592	    purposes_fact = facts.facts.intent_purposes
   593	    if purposes_fact.status == "KNOWN":
   594	        values = purposes_fact.value
   595	        if len(values) == 1:
   596	            derived = _VISA_PURPOSE_TO_REQUEST_CATEGORY.get(values[0], "other")
   597	    if derived != "other":
   598	        return derived
   599	    return hint if hint is not None else "other"
   600

   602	def build_temp_unavailable_body(
   603	    *,
   604	    now: datetime,
   605	    code: str,
   606	    mode: EngineMode | None = None,
   607	) -> dict[str, JsonValue]:
   608	    """The TEMPORARILY_UNAVAILABLE-shaped envelope body (HTTP 200).
   609	
   610	    Returned — with no successful decision claimed — whenever evaluation cannot run:
   611	    surface disabled (OFF), no active pack, pack verification/compilation
   612	    failure, or the crypto/evaluation layer fail-closing. ``mode`` is still
   613	    ``resolve_response_mode()`` so callers can distinguish comparison-only
   614	    SHADOW responses from authoritative ENFORCE responses.
   615	
   616	    ``facts_fingerprint`` is null because no evaluation happened; fabricating
   617	    an HMAC tag over unevaluated facts would be a dishonest integrity claim.
   618	    """
   619	
   620	    iso_now = now.astimezone(timezone.utc).isoformat()
   980	
   981	def _attach_price_quotes(
   982	    decision: Decision,
   983	    compiled: CompiledRulePack,
   984	    *,
   985	    pricing_catalog: ExactPricingCatalog,
   986	) -> Decision:
   987	    """Attach exact-key PricingTool quotes before decision sealing/persistence."""
   988	
   989	    if decision.state is not DecisionState.SUPPORTED_CANDIDATES:
   990	        return decision
   991	    if decision.decision_id is None:  # pragma: no cover - evaluated-state invariant
   992	        return decision
   993	    products = {
   994	        product.product_version_id: product for product in compiled.source_pack.payload.products
   995	    }
   996	    quotes = []
   997	    for candidate in decision.candidates:
   998	        product = products.get(candidate.product_version_id)
   999	        if product is None:
  1000	            continue
  1001	        resolution = resolve_candidate_pricing(
  1002	            product,
  1003	            pricing_catalog=pricing_catalog,
  1004	            evaluated_at=decision.evaluated_at,
  1005	        )
  1006	        quote = build_price_quote(product, resolution, decision_id=decision.decision_id)
  1007	        if quote is not None:
  1008	            quotes.append(quote)
  1009	    payload = decision.model_dump(mode="python")
  1010	    payload["quotes"] = tuple(quotes)
  1011	    return Decision.model_validate(payload)

  1033	def _apply_minor_privacy_hold(decision: Decision, facts: ApplicantFacts) -> Decision:
  1034	    """Apply Privacy Policy V1's non-eligibility guardian safety boundary.
  1035	
  1036	    The public evaluation contract has no guardian-identity/consent fact, so a
  1037	    known minor can never prove that an automated supported outcome is safe.
  1038	    This deterministic adapter may only abstain: it cannot create, retain or
  1039	    reorder a candidate. Empty citations are intentional because this is a
  1040	    product/privacy workflow control, not a claim of legal visa ineligibility.
  1041	    """
  1042	
  1043	    if decision.state is DecisionState.TEMPORARILY_UNAVAILABLE:
  1044	        return decision
  1045	    snapshot = DEFAULT_FACT_REGISTRY.derive(facts, effective_at=decision.effective_at)
  1046	    minor_fact = snapshot.values[FactPath.DERIVED_IS_MINOR]
  1047	    if isinstance(minor_fact, UnknownFact):
  1048	        if decision.state is DecisionState.HUMAN_REVIEW_REQUIRED:
  1049	            return decision
  1050	        missing = tuple(
  1051	            sorted(
  1052	                {*decision.missing_facts, FactPath.PERSON_BIRTH_DATE},
  1053	                key=lambda path: path.value,
  1054	            )
  1055	        )
  1056	        payload = decision.model_dump(mode="python")
  1057	        payload.update(
  1058	            {
  1059	                "state": "NEEDS_INPUT",
  1060	                "candidates": (),
  1061	                "missing_facts": missing,
  1062	                "review_reasons": (),
  1063	                "no_path_reasons": (),
  1064	                "outage": None,
  1065	                "quotes": (),
  1066	                "decision_integrity": None,
  1067	            }
  1068	        )
  1069	        return Decision.model_validate(payload)
  1070	    if minor_fact.value is not True:
  1071	        return decision
  1072	
  1073	    reason = Reason(
  1074	        code="MINOR_GUARDIAN_PRIVACY_REVIEW",
  1075	        rule_ids=("system.privacy.minor-guardian-review",),
  1076	        source_refs=(),
  1077	    )
  1078	    existing_reasons = (
  1079	        decision.review_reasons if decision.state is DecisionState.HUMAN_REVIEW_REQUIRED else ()
  1080	    )
  1081	    payload = decision.model_dump(mode="python")
  1082	    payload.update(
  1083	        {
  1084	            "state": "HUMAN_REVIEW_REQUIRED",
  1085	            "candidates": (),
  1086	            "missing_facts": (),
  1087	            "review_reasons": (*existing_reasons, reason),
  1088	            "no_path_reasons": (),
  1089	            "outage": None,
  1090	            "quotes": (),
  1091	            "decision_integrity": None,
  1092	        }
  1093	    )
  1094	    return Decision.model_validate(payload)
  1095

  1097	def _apply_decisive_source_authority_hold(
  1098	    decision: Decision,
  1099	    compiled: CompiledRulePack,
  1100	) -> Decision:
  1101	    """Abstain unless every decisive citation is authoritative at both clocks.
  1102	
  1103	    This runs after deterministic evaluation but before sealing/persistence.
  1104	    It is deliberately independent of ``Rule.safety_critical``: no supported
  1105	    candidate or definitive no-path result may rely on a secondary, revoked,
  1106	    superseded, unavailable, legally inapplicable, system-time-inapplicable,
  1107	    or non-current source.
  1108	    """
  1109	
  1110	    if decision.state not in (
  1111	        DecisionState.SUPPORTED_CANDIDATES,
  1112	        DecisionState.NO_SUPPORTED_PATH,
  1113	    ):
  1114	        return decision

   691	def assert_only_expected_changes(before: dict[str, Any], after: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
   692	    """Fail-closed on both axes: name what MAY move and require universal
   693	    equality for everything else, so a key added in some future sequence is
   694	    guarded automatically rather than escaping an allow-list."""
   695	    if set(after) != set(before):
   696	        _fail(
   697	            "the payload's top-level key set changed "
   698	            f"(added {sorted(set(after) - set(before))}, "
   699	            f"removed {sorted(set(before) - set(after))})"
   700	        )
   701	    for key in set(before) - _IDENTITY_KEYS - {"rules"}:
   702	        if _canon(after.get(key)) != _canon(before.get(key)):
   703	            _fail(f"{key} changed — this fold retires and inserts rules and nothing else")
   704	
   705	    before_rules = _rules_by_id(before)
   706	    after_rules = _rules_by_id(after)
   707	
   708	    missing = set(before_rules) - set(after_rules)
   709	    if missing != set(RETIRED_REVIEW_RULES):
   710	        _fail(
   711	            f"removed-rule set mismatch: {sorted(missing)} != "
   712	            f"{sorted(RETIRED_REVIEW_RULES)}"
   713	        )
   714	    added = set(after_rules) - set(before_rules)
   715	    if added != set(NEW_RULE_IDS):
   716	        _fail(f"added-rule set mismatch: {sorted(added)} != {sorted(NEW_RULE_IDS)}")
   717	
   718	    for rule_id, rule in after_rules.items():
   719	        if rule_id in set(NEW_RULE_IDS):
   720	            continue
   721	        if _canon(rule) != _canon(before_rules[rule_id]):
   722	            _fail(
   723	                f"rule {rule_id!r} drifted from seq-20 — this fold edits NO existing "
   724	                "rule, it only retires nine and inserts eleven"
   725	            )
   726	
   727	
   728	def assert_changed_fields_hold_their_expected_values(
   729	    after: dict[str, Any], *, expected_new_rules: list[dict[str, Any]]
   730	) -> None:
   731	    """:func:`assert_only_expected_changes` names what MAY move and excludes it
   732	    from comparison — silent on whether it moved to the RIGHT thing. Pinned
   733	    separately, per the lesson seq-18's review recorded: a guard whose
   734	    fail-closedness holds only while the code above it stays correct is not a
   735	    guard, it is a comment."""
   736	    expected: dict[str, Any] = {
   737	        "sequence": 21,
   738	        "rule_pack_id": str(_rule_pack_id(21)),
   739	        "version": FOLD_VERSION,
   740	        "created_at": FOLD_CREATED_AT,
   741	        "created_by": FOLD_CREATED_BY,
   742	        "valid_period": {"to": None, "from": PACK_VALID_FROM},
   743	        "previous_payload_sha256": SEQ20_PAYLOAD_SHA256,
   744	        "rollback_of_payload_sha256": None,
   745	    }
   746	    for key, want in expected.items():
   747	        got = after.get(key)
   748	        if got != want:
   749	            _fail(f"{key} is {got!r}, expected {want!r}")
   750	
   751	    rules_by_id = _rules_by_id(after)
   752	    for rule_id in RETIRED_REVIEW_RULES:
   753	        if rule_id in rules_by_id:
   754	            _fail(f"rule {rule_id!r} should have been retired but is still present")
   755	
   756	    by_id = {rule["rule_id"]: rule for rule in expected_new_rules}
   757	    for rule_id in NEW_RULE_IDS:
   758	        if _canon(rules_by_id.get(rule_id)) != _canon(by_id[rule_id]):
   759	            _fail(f"{rule_id!r} in the output is not the rule this fold built")
   760	
   761	    # Every target product now has exactly one ELIGIBILITY rule, and it reads
   762	    # that product's own qualifying fact. Stated as an OUTPUT census rather
   763	    # than as nine assertions, so a row added to SUPPORT_RULES without a
   764	    # matching product is caught here too.
   765	    for row in SUPPORT_RULES:
   766	        eligibility = _eligibility_rule_ids_for_product(after, row["product_code"])
   767	        if eligibility != {row["rule_id"]}:
   768	            _fail(
   769	                f"product {row['product_code']!r} ends the fold with ELIGIBILITY "
   770	                f"rules {sorted(eligibility)}, expected exactly [{row['rule_id']!r}]"
   771	            )
   772	        facts = rules_by_id[row["rule_id"]]["required_facts"]
   773	        if row["qualifying_fact"] not in facts:
   774	            _fail(
   775	                f"{row['rule_id']!r} does not read its qualifying fact "
   776	                f"{row['qualifying_fact']!r} — a SUPPORT rule keyed on sponsor "
   777	                "category alone is the exact defect this fold exists to cure"
   778	            )
   779	
   780	
   781	def fold(
   782	    seq20: dict[str, Any],
   783	    seq20_signed: dict[str, Any],
   784	    *,
   785	    observed_at: datetime | None = None,
   786	) -> dict[str, Any]:
   787	    """Return the seq-21 payload, or abort loudly.
   788	
   789	    ``seq20_signed`` is the signed seq-20 envelope and is REQUIRED, not
   790	    optional — see :func:`assert_anchor_is_a_verified_signed_artifact`.
   790	    optional — see :func:`assert_anchor_is_a_verified_signed_artifact`.
   791	    ``observed_at`` is threaded into that signature check's clock so a test
   792	    pinning it is not left real-clock-dependent.
   793	    """
   794	    digest = hashlib.sha256(canonicalize_json(seq20)).hexdigest()
   795	    if digest != SEQ20_PAYLOAD_SHA256:
   796	        _fail(
   797	            "the seq-20 source is not the activated artifact: recomputed JCS "
   798	            f"digest {digest} != {SEQ20_PAYLOAD_SHA256}. Everything below would "
   799	            "otherwise be built on a payload production never ran."
   800	        )
   801	    assert_anchor_is_a_verified_signed_artifact(seq20_signed, digest, observed_at=observed_at)
   802	    if seq20.get("sequence") != 20:
   803	        _fail(f"expected sequence 20, got {seq20.get('sequence')!r}")
   804	
   805	    inherited_id = seq20.get("rule_pack_id")
   806	    expected_20_id = str(_rule_pack_id(20))
   807	    if inherited_id != expected_20_id:
   808	        _fail(
   809	            f"the seq-20 payload carries rule_pack_id={inherited_id!r}, but the "
   810	            f"uuid5 convention yields {expected_20_id!r} — the anchor is verified, "
   811	            "never assumed."
   812	        )
   813	    collisions = sorted(set(NEW_RULE_IDS) & set(_rules_by_id(seq20)))
   814	    if collisions:
   815	        _fail(f"rule(s) {collisions} already exist in seq-20 — this fold declares them as INSERTs")
   816	
   817	    _assert_target_products_have_no_eligibility_rule(seq20)
   818	    _assert_retired_review_rules_are_dormant(seq20)
   819	    _assert_employment_sponsor_scope_is_coherent(seq20)
   820	
   821	    new_rules = build_new_rules(seq20)
   822	
   823	    out = json.loads(json.dumps(seq20))
   824	    out["rules"] = [rule for rule in out["rules"] if rule["rule_id"] not in RETIRED_REVIEW_RULES]
   825	    out["rules"].extend(copy.deepcopy(rule) for rule in new_rules)
   826	
   827	    out["sequence"] = 21
   828	    out["rule_pack_id"] = str(_rule_pack_id(21))
   829	    out["version"] = FOLD_VERSION
   830	    out["created_at"] = FOLD_CREATED_AT
   831	    out["created_by"] = FOLD_CREATED_BY
   832	    out["valid_period"] = {"to": None, "from": PACK_VALID_FROM}
   833	    out["previous_payload_sha256"] = SEQ20_PAYLOAD_SHA256
   834	    out["rollback_of_payload_sha256"] = None
   835	
   836	    assert_only_expected_changes(seq20, out)
   837	    assert_changed_fields_hold_their_expected_values(out, expected_new_rules=new_rules)
   838	    RulePackPayload.model_validate(out)
   839	    return out
   840	
   841	
   842	def _assert_output_does_not_collide_with_inputs(output: Path, input_paths: dict[str, Path]) -> None:
   843	    """Refuse to write ``--output`` onto any input path, and refuse an output
   844	    path that merely LOOKS like a signed artifact — verbatim the guard
   845	    ``fold_pack_seq20.py`` carries, for the same reason: a copy-pasted flag
   846	    could otherwise overwrite the SIGNED production anchor with unsigned fold
   847	    bytes."""
   848	    resolved_output = output.resolve()
   849	    for flag, path in input_paths.items():
   850	        if resolved_output == path.resolve():
   851	            _fail(
   852	                f"--output {output} resolves to the same file as {flag} "
   853	                f"({path}) — refusing to overwrite an input (or the signed "
   854	                "production anchor) with unsigned fold output"
   855	            )
   856	    if resolved_output.name.endswith(".signed.json"):
   857	        _fail(
   858	            f"--output {output} ends in '.signed.json' — this script only "
   859	            "ever writes an unsigned SOURCE file (see the module docstring); "
   860	            "refusing to write unsigned bytes to a path that looks signed"
   861	        )
   862	
   863	
   864	def main(argv: list[str] | None = None, *, observed_at: datetime | None = None) -> int:
   865	    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Fold RulePack seq-21.")
   866	    parser.add_argument("--seq20-source", required=True, type=Path)
   867	    parser.add_argument(
   868	        "--seq20-signed",
   869	        type=Path,
   870	        default=None,
   871	        help=(
   872	            "the signed seq-20 envelope; defaults to the .signed.json sibling "
   873	            "of --seq20-source. Its signature is verified — the anchor is "
   874	            "never taken on the digest constant alone."
   875	        ),
   876	    )
   877	    parser.add_argument("--output", required=True, type=Path)
   878	    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
   879	
   880	    if args.seq20_signed is not None:
   881	        signed_path = args.seq20_signed
   882	    else:
   883	        source_str = str(args.seq20_source)
   884	        if not source_str.endswith(".source.json"):
   885	            _fail(
   886	                f"--seq20-source {source_str!r} does not end in '.source.json' — "
   887	                "cannot derive the signed sibling path; pass --seq20-signed explicitly"
   888	            )
   889	        signed_path = Path(source_str[: -len(".source.json")] + ".signed.json")
   890	    if signed_path == args.seq20_source or not signed_path.exists():
   891	        _fail(f"no signed seq-20 bundle at {signed_path} — pass --seq20-signed")
   892	
   893	    _assert_output_does_not_collide_with_inputs(
   894	        args.output,
   895	        {"--seq20-source": args.seq20_source, "--seq20-signed": signed_path},
   896	    )
   897	
   898	    seq20 = json.loads(args.seq20_source.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
   899	    seq20_signed = json.loads(signed_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
   900	    seq21 = fold(seq20, seq20_signed, observed_at=observed_at)
   901	    args.output.write_text(json.dumps(seq21, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
   902	    digest = hashlib.sha256(canonicalize_json(seq21)).hexdigest()
   903	    print(f"fold_pack_seq21: wrote {args.output}")
   904	    print(f"fold_pack_seq21: seq-21 payload_sha256 = {digest}")
   905	    print(f"fold_pack_seq21: retired {sorted(RETIRED_REVIEW_RULES)}")
   906	    print(f"fold_pack_seq21: inserted {sorted(NEW_RULE_IDS)}")
   907	    print("fold_pack_seq21: NOT SIGNED, NOT ACTIVATED — see sign_pack.py / activate_pack.py")
   908	    return 0
   909	
   910	
   911	if __name__ == "__main__":
   912	    sys.exit(main())

   333	def _evaluate_stage(rules: Sequence[CompiledRule], facts: FactSnapshot) -> tuple[_StageResult, ...]:
   334	    """Evaluate every rule in one stage against ``facts``. Never short-circuits
   335	    across rules (each rule's own ``evaluate_condition`` already never
   336	    short-circuits within itself — spec §4.1)."""
   337	    return tuple((rule, ast_module.evaluate_condition(rule.when, facts)) for rule in rules)

   340	def _safety_unknowns(entries: Sequence[_StageResult]) -> tuple[_StageResult, ...]:
   341	    """The subset of ``entries`` whose condition is UNKNOWN and whose rule
   342	    does not declare ``on_unknown=NO_EFFECT`` — i.e. an UNKNOWN result that
   343	    the rule author says *could* still change the outcome once resolved
   344	    (whether by asking the applicant, per ``NEEDS_INPUT``, or by escalating
   345	    to a human reviewer, per ``HUMAN_REVIEW`` — see
   346	    ``_partition_unknowns_by_policy`` for that split).
   347	    """
   348	    return tuple(
   349	        (rule, result)
   350	        for rule, result in entries
   351	        if result.truth is TruthValue.UNKNOWN and rule.on_unknown is not OnUnknownAction.NO_EFFECT
   352	    )
   353	
   354	
   355	def _partition_unknowns_by_policy(
   356	    entries: Sequence[_StageResult],
   357	) -> tuple[tuple[_StageResult, ...], tuple[_StageResult, ...]]:
   358	    """Split an already-``_safety_unknowns``-filtered sequence into
   359	    ``(review_unknowns, input_unknowns)`` by each rule's own ``on_unknown``
   360	    policy (gate round 1 item 4, 2026-07-19 — ``on_unknown=HUMAN_REVIEW`` was
   361	    previously a dead option, silently treated identically to
   362	    ``NEEDS_INPUT``).
   363	
   364	    A ``HUMAN_REVIEW``-tagged UNKNOWN contributes a review reason: the rule
   365	    author is saying "if we cannot determine this, put it in front of a
   366	    human — do not just ask the applicant for more facts". A
   367	    ``NEEDS_INPUT``-tagged UNKNOWN contributes a missing fact, exactly as
   368	    before.
   369	    """
   370	    review = tuple(
   371	        entry for entry in entries if entry[0].on_unknown is OnUnknownAction.HUMAN_REVIEW
   372	    )
   373	    needs_input = tuple(
   374	        entry for entry in entries if entry[0].on_unknown is OnUnknownAction.NEEDS_INPUT
   375	    )
   376	    return review, needs_input
   377

   379	def _sorted_uuids(values: Iterable[uuid.UUID]) -> tuple[uuid.UUID, ...]:
   380	    return tuple(sorted(set(values), key=str))

   383	def _reason_from_rule(rule: CompiledRule) -> Reason:
   384	    """Build one ``Reason`` from a rule whose effect fired (EXCLUDE or
   385	    REQUIRE_REVIEW), or whose UNKNOWN result escalated to review under
   386	    ``on_unknown=HUMAN_REVIEW`` — citations propagated verbatim from the
   387	    rule either way.
   388	    """
   389	    return Reason(
   390	        code=rule.effect.reason_code,  # type: ignore[union-attr]
   391	        rule_ids=(rule.rule_id,),
   392	        source_refs=_sorted_uuids(rule.source_refs),
   393	    )

   396	def _true_reasons(entries: Sequence[_StageResult]) -> tuple[Reason, ...]:
   397	    """One ``Reason`` per rule whose condition evaluated definitely TRUE."""
   398	    return tuple(
   399	        _reason_from_rule(rule) for rule, result in entries if result.truth is TruthValue.TRUE
