   403	def _unknown_reasons(entries: Sequence[_StageResult]) -> tuple[Reason, ...]:
   404	    """One ``Reason`` per rule in an UNKNOWN-but-escalated-to-review bucket
   405	    (``on_unknown=HUMAN_REVIEW``, see ``_partition_unknowns_by_policy``) —
   406	    reuses the rule's own ``reason_code``/citations exactly like
   407	    ``_true_reasons`` does for a definite TRUE, since the rule author
   408	    declared this particular UNKNOWN itself review-worthy.
   409	    """
   410	    return tuple(_reason_from_rule(rule) for rule, _ in entries)
   411	
   412	
   413	def _dedupe_reasons(reasons: Iterable[Reason]) -> tuple[Reason, ...]:
   414	    """Collapse duplicate ``Reason``s (same code/rule_ids/source_refs) that
   415	    arise when the same GLOBAL rule fires identically across several
   416	    products — first-seen order preserved for determinism.
   417	    """
   418	    seen: dict[tuple[str, tuple[str, ...], tuple[str, ...]], Reason] = {}
   419	    for reason in reasons:
   420	        key = (
   421	            reason.code,
   422	            tuple(reason.rule_ids),
   423	            tuple(str(ref) for ref in reason.source_refs),
   424	        )
   425	        seen.setdefault(key, reason)
   426	    return tuple(seen.values())
   427	
   428	
   429	def merge_reasons_by_code(reasons: Iterable[Reason]) -> tuple[Reason, ...]:
   430	    """Collapse ``Reason``s that render as the SAME SENTENCE — one entry per
   627	# Per-product proof (spec §4.2 ``evaluate_product``)
   628	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   629	
   630	
   631	def evaluate_product(
   632	    *,
   633	    product: CompiledProduct,
   634	    rules: Sequence[CompiledRule],
   635	    facts: FactSnapshot,
   636	    purposes: frozenset[str],
   637	    fact_registry: FactRegistry = DEFAULT_FACT_REGISTRY,
   638	    _trace_sink: list[_TraceEntry] | None = None,
   639	) -> ProductProof:
   640	    """Evaluate one product's HARD_FILTER -> HUMAN_REVIEW -> ELIGIBILITY
   641	    stage loop (spec §4.2, verbatim algorithm — the docstring order matches
   642	    ``enums.STAGE_ORDER``, not ``RuleStage``'s declaration order).
   643	
   644	    ``rules`` must already be the product-specific, in-force, sorted rule
   645	    sequence (``CompiledRulePack.rules_for(product, effective_at=...)``).
   646	
   647	    Escalation precedence within one product (gate round 1 item 4, see
   648	    module docstring): a stage's own definite TRUE always wins first
   649	    (EXCLUDED / REVIEW); next, any ``on_unknown=HUMAN_REVIEW`` UNKNOWN from
   650	    HARD_FILTER or HUMAN_REVIEW escalates straight to REVIEW — a rule author
   651	    asking for human judgment on an uncertain exclusion/review trigger
   652	    outranks merely asking the applicant for more facts; only then do
   653	    ``on_unknown=NEEDS_INPUT`` UNKNOWNs from those two stages block via
   654	    BLOCKED_UNKNOWN. ELIGIBILITY runs last and applies the same
   655	    review-before-input precedence to whichever unknown SUPPORT rules are
   656	    actually relevant to the remaining purpose gap (see the
   657	    ``potential_coverage`` computation below, gate round 1 item 1 / P0-A).
   658	    """
   659	    by_stage = _rules_by_stage(rules)
   660	
   661	    # Evaluate all proof stages before applying precedence. Conditions are
   662	    # pure and compiler-validated, so the verdict is unchanged; unlike the
   663	    # old cross-stage short-circuit this produces a complete audit traversal.
   664	    # RANKING remains restricted to supported products in ``_rank_supported``.
   665	    hard_results = _evaluate_stage(by_stage.get(RuleStage.HARD_FILTER, ()), facts)
   666	    review_results = _evaluate_stage(by_stage.get(RuleStage.HUMAN_REVIEW, ()), facts)
   667	    support_results = _evaluate_stage(by_stage.get(RuleStage.ELIGIBILITY, ()), facts)
   668	
   669	    # PR-2 gate follow-up (2026-09-06): the STRUCTURAL purpose-coverage claim
   670	    # of this product, computed above every early return so that
   671	    # `purpose_feasible` rides on EVERY proof this function can produce —
   672	    # including the EXCLUDED and REVIEW ones that return long before the
   673	    # fact-dependent `naive_potential_coverage` test further down. It is the
   674	    # union of `covered_purposes` over ALL in-force ELIGIBILITY rules
   675	    # regardless of truth value (`STAGE_EFFECT_TYPE` guarantees every
   676	    # ELIGIBILITY rule carries an `EffectSupport`), so a product with zero
   677	    # ELIGIBILITY rules — E33A/B/C, E23U/V, E28B/C/D/F under seq-19 — claims
   678	    # nothing and is feasible for nobody. Pure: no rule is evaluated here
   679	    # that `_evaluate_stage` did not already evaluate above.
   680	    declared_coverage: frozenset[str] = (
   681	        frozenset[str]().union(
   682	            *(frozenset(rule.effect.covered_purposes) for rule, _ in support_results)  # type: ignore[union-attr]
   683	        )
   684	        if support_results
   685	        else frozenset()
   686	    )
   687	    purpose_feasible = purposes <= declared_coverage
   688	
   689	    def finish(
   690	        proof: ProductProof,
   691	        *,
   692	        applied_rule_ids: frozenset[str],
   693	    ) -> ProductProof:
   694	        proof = replace(proof, purpose_feasible=purpose_feasible)
   695	        if _trace_sink is not None:
   696	            for rule, result in hard_results + review_results + support_results:
   697	                _trace_sink.append(
   698	                    _TraceEntry(
   699	                        rule=rule,
   700	                        result=result,
   701	                        product_version_id=product.product_version_id,
   702	                        evaluation_scope="PRODUCT_PROOF",
   703	                        product_proof_status=proof.status,
   704	                        applied_effect=(
   705	                            _effect_for_result(rule, result)
   706	                            if rule.rule_id in applied_rule_ids
   707	                            else None
   708	                        ),
   709	                    )
   710	                )
   711	        return proof
   712	
   713	    if any(result.truth is TruthValue.TRUE for _, result in hard_results):
   714	        return finish(
   715	            ProductProof(
   716	                product=product,
   717	                status=ProductProofStatus.EXCLUDED,
   718	                reasons=_true_reasons(hard_results),
   719	            ),
   720	            applied_rule_ids=frozenset(
   721	                rule.rule_id for rule, result in hard_results if result.truth is TruthValue.TRUE
   722	            ),
   723	        )
   724	    hard_safety = _safety_unknowns(hard_results)
   725	    hard_review_unknowns, hard_input_unknowns = _partition_unknowns_by_policy(hard_safety)
   726	
   727	    if any(result.truth is TruthValue.TRUE for _, result in review_results):
   728	        return finish(
   729	            ProductProof(
   730	                product=product,
   731	                status=ProductProofStatus.REVIEW,
   732	                reasons=_true_reasons(review_results),
   733	            ),
   734	            applied_rule_ids=frozenset(
   735	                rule.rule_id for rule, result in review_results if result.truth is TruthValue.TRUE
   736	            ),
   737	        )
   738	    review_safety = _safety_unknowns(review_results)
   739	    review_review_unknowns, review_input_unknowns = _partition_unknowns_by_policy(review_safety)
   740	
   741	    if hard_review_unknowns or review_review_unknowns:
   742	        return finish(
   743	            ProductProof(
   744	                product=product,
   745	                status=ProductProofStatus.REVIEW,
   746	                reasons=_unknown_reasons(hard_review_unknowns + review_review_unknowns),
   747	            ),
   748	            applied_rule_ids=frozenset(
   749	                rule.rule_id for rule, _ in hard_review_unknowns + review_review_unknowns
   750	            ),
   751	        )
   752	
   753	    true_support = tuple(
   754	        (rule, result) for rule, result in support_results if result.truth is TruthValue.TRUE
   755	    )
   756	    covered: frozenset[str] = (
   757	        frozenset[str]().union(
   758	            *(frozenset(rule.effect.covered_purposes) for rule, _ in true_support)  # type: ignore[union-attr]
   759	        )
   760	        if true_support
   761	        else frozenset()
   762	    )
   763	    support_safety = _safety_unknowns(support_results)
   764	    support_review_unknowns, support_input_unknowns = _partition_unknowns_by_policy(support_safety)
   765	
   766	    # P0-A fix (gate round 1 item 1, see module docstring): the previous
   767	    # check asked "does ANY unknown SUPPORT rule's covered_purposes
   768	    # intersect ANY missing purpose" — wrong whenever one missing purpose is
   769	    # permanently uncoverable by anything in this product while ANOTHER is
   770	    # potentially coverable via an unknown rule. `naive_potential_coverage`
   771	    # below (the optimistic union, ignoring joint consistency) still answers
   772	    # exactly that question: any purpose it can't reach is permanently
   773	    # uncoverable by ANYTHING in this product, full stop, regardless of how
   774	    # any fact resolves — reported verbatim as `missing_purposes` here,
   775	    # unchanged from round 1.
   776	    #
   777	    # Decisiveness reorder (2026-09-06, research/visa/
   778	    # 2026-09-06-visa-oracle-decisiveness-investigation.md §4 PR-2): this
   779	    # test runs BEFORE the `hard_input_unknowns or review_input_unknowns`
   780	    # block below, not after it. A product whose SUPPORT rules can never
   781	    # cover the applicant's declared purposes must not get to name the fact
   782	    # the applicant is asked for — `evaluate`'s
   783	    # `min(blocked, key=len(missing_facts))` tie-break otherwise lets a
   784	    # product with ZERO SUPPORT rules (E33A/B/C, E23U/V, E28B/C/D/F under
   785	    # seq-19) choose the global `NEEDS_INPUT` question for everybody else.
   786	    # This is a REORDER, not a new computation: `covered`, `support_safety`
   787	    # and `purposes` are all already resolved above. It cannot fail open —
   788	    # the only status it can return is UNSUPPORTED, so the reachable
   789	    # behaviour change is `NEEDS_INPUT` → the honest `NO_SUPPORTED_PATH`,
   790	    # never `NEEDS_INPUT` → `SUPPORTED`, and every EXCLUDED/REVIEW return
   791	    # above still runs first. Pinned by
   792	    # `test_evaluator_purpose_feasibility_precedence.py`.
   793	    naive_potential_coverage: frozenset[str] = covered | (
   794	        frozenset[str]().union(
   795	            *(frozenset(rule.effect.covered_purposes) for rule, _ in support_safety)  # type: ignore[union-attr]
   796	        )
   797	        if support_safety
   798	        else frozenset()
   799	    )
   800	    if not (purposes <= naive_potential_coverage):
   801	        return finish(
   802	            ProductProof(
   803	                product=product,
   804	                status=ProductProofStatus.UNSUPPORTED,
   805	                missing_purposes=purposes - naive_potential_coverage,
   806	            ),
   807	            applied_rule_ids=frozenset(rule.rule_id for rule, _ in true_support),
   808	        )
   809	
   810	    if hard_input_unknowns or review_input_unknowns:
   811	        missing = _underlying_applicant_facts(
   812	            hard_input_unknowns + review_input_unknowns, fact_registry
   813	        )
   814	        return finish(
   815	            ProductProof(
   816	                product=product,
   817	                status=ProductProofStatus.BLOCKED_UNKNOWN,
   818	                missing_facts=missing,
   819	            ),
   820	            applied_rule_ids=frozenset(
   821	                rule.rule_id for rule, _ in hard_input_unknowns + review_input_unknowns
   822	            ),
   823	        )
   824	
   825	    if purposes <= covered:
   826	        return finish(
   827	            ProductProof(
   828	                product=product,
   829	                status=ProductProofStatus.SUPPORTED,
   830	                support_rules=tuple(rule for rule, _ in true_support),
   831	                covered_purposes=covered,
   832	            ),
   833	            applied_rule_ids=frozenset(rule.rule_id for rule, _ in true_support),
   834	        )
   835	
   836	    missing_purposes = purposes - covered
   837	
   838	    # Gate round 2 (2026-07-20) P0-R2: the optimistic union above says every
   839	    # purpose is INDIVIDUALLY reachable by some unknown rule — but it never
   840	    # asked whether those rules can all be TRUE at the same time. That is
   841	    # itself a Strong-Kleene violation whenever two of them can never both
   842	    # hold at once (e.g. one requires `marital_status == MARRIED` to cover
   843	    # TOURISM, another requires `marital_status == SINGLE` to cover STUDY:
   844	    # no resolution of `marital_status` ever covers both, yet the union
   845	    # claimed it did, making the UNKNOWN case strictly MORE favorable than
   846	    # every one of its own possible concrete resolutions).
   847	    # `_has_consistent_covering_subset` requires at least one JOINTLY
   848	    # CONSISTENT covering subset of the unknown rules, not just a bare
   849	    # union. If none exists, the product is definitively UNSUPPORTED right
   850	    # now — no single future resolution could ever realize the coverage the
   851	    # naive union promised.
   852	    if not _has_consistent_covering_subset(missing_purposes, support_safety):
   853	        return finish(
   854	            ProductProof(
   855	                product=product,
   856	                status=ProductProofStatus.UNSUPPORTED,
   857	                missing_purposes=missing_purposes,
   858	            ),
   859	            applied_rule_ids=frozenset(rule.rule_id for rule, _ in true_support),
   860	        )
   861	
   862	    # Every declared purpose IS potentially coverable by some jointly
   863	    # consistent combination of unknown SUPPORT rules — scope the decision
   864	    # to the unknown SUPPORT rules that actually touch the remaining gap (an
   865	    # unknown rule covering a purpose the applicant never declared must not
   866	    # drive either bucket). Review-tagged relevance wins over input-tagged,
   867	    # consistent with the review-before-input precedence used above.
   868	    relevant_review = tuple(
   869	        entry
   870	        for entry in support_review_unknowns
   871	        if frozenset(entry[0].effect.covered_purposes) & missing_purposes  # type: ignore[union-attr]
   872	    )
   873	    relevant_input = tuple(
   874	        entry
   875	        for entry in support_input_unknowns
   876	        if frozenset(entry[0].effect.covered_purposes) & missing_purposes  # type: ignore[union-attr]
   877	    )
   878	    if relevant_review:
   879	        return finish(
   880	            ProductProof(
   881	                product=product,
   882	                status=ProductProofStatus.REVIEW,
   883	                reasons=_unknown_reasons(relevant_review),
   884	            ),
   885	            applied_rule_ids=frozenset(rule.rule_id for rule, _ in true_support + relevant_review),
   886	        )
   887	    missing = _underlying_applicant_facts(relevant_input, fact_registry)
   888	    return finish(
   889	        ProductProof(
   890	            product=product,
  1400	
  1401	    # --- GLOBAL HUMAN_REVIEW pre-pass (gate round 1 item 3 / P0-C, see
  1402	    # module docstring) — evaluated ONCE, here, before purpose extraction
  1403	    # and before the per-product loop. `rules_for()` only ever surfaces a
  1404	    # GLOBAL rule when called FOR a specific product, so this cannot be
  1405	    # expressed as "just call rules_for" without a product to loop over —
  1406	    # the three reachable counterexamples this fixes (unknown purposes,
  1407	    # zero active products, a GLOBAL hard-filter excluding every product
  1408	    # first) are covered by `test_evaluator_gate_round1.py`. A TRUE result
  1409	    # here wins unconditionally at final assembly (frozen precedence), while
  1410	    # the product-proof traversal still completes when purposes are known so
  1411	    # the trace is not truncated. This does not replace the per-product stage —
  1412	    # PRODUCTS-scoped review rules, and a GLOBAL rule that resolves UNKNOWN
  1413	    # under `on_unknown` policies other than HUMAN_REVIEW, still flow
  1414	    # through `evaluate_product()` below exactly as before.
  1415	    #
  1416	    # Gate round 2 (2026-07-20) — P0-R1: an UNKNOWN result here used to be
  1417	    # silently dropped, so a GLOBAL review rule tagged `on_unknown=
  1418	    # HUMAN_REVIEW` never escalated when its own condition could not be
  1419	    # determined — precisely the case `on_unknown=HUMAN_REVIEW` exists to
  1420	    # cover ("if we can't tell, a human must look"). Fixed by ALSO
  1421	    # collecting UNKNOWN entries whose rule opts into HUMAN_REVIEW, exactly
  1422	    # mirroring the per-product `_partition_unknowns_by_policy` split.
  1423	    global_review_rules = sorted(
  1424	        (
  1425	            rule
  1426	            for rule in compiled_pack.rules
  1427	            if rule.scope is RuleScope.GLOBAL
  1428	            and rule.stage is RuleStage.HUMAN_REVIEW
  1429	            and _period_contains(rule.source_rule.valid_period, effective_at)
  1430	        ),
  1431	        key=lambda rule: (rule.priority, rule.rule_id),
  1432	    )
  1433	    global_review_results = _evaluate_stage(global_review_rules, snapshot)
  1434	    trace_entries.extend(
  1435	        _TraceEntry(
  1436	            rule=rule,
  1437	            result=result,
  1438	            product_version_id=None,
  1439	            evaluation_scope="GLOBAL_PREPASS",
  1440	            product_proof_status=None,
  1441	            applied_effect=(
  1442	                _effect_for_result(rule, result)
  1443	                if result.truth is TruthValue.TRUE
  1444	                or (
  1445	                    result.truth is TruthValue.UNKNOWN
  1446	                    and rule.on_unknown is OnUnknownAction.HUMAN_REVIEW
  1447	                )
  1448	                else None
  1449	            ),
  1450	        )
  1451	        for rule, result in global_review_results
  1452	    )
  1453	    global_true_entries = tuple(
  1454	        (rule, result) for rule, result in global_review_results if result.truth is TruthValue.TRUE
  1455	    )
  1456	    global_unknown_review_entries = tuple(
  1457	        (rule, result)
  1458	        for rule, result in global_review_results
  1459	        if result.truth is TruthValue.UNKNOWN and rule.on_unknown is OnUnknownAction.HUMAN_REVIEW
  1460	    )
  1461	    global_review_reasons: tuple[Reason, ...] = ()
  1462	    if global_true_entries or global_unknown_review_entries:
  1463	        global_review_reasons = _dedupe_reasons(
  1464	            _true_reasons(global_true_entries) + _unknown_reasons(global_unknown_review_entries)
  1465	        )
  1466	
  1467	    purposes_fact = snapshot.values.get(FactPath.INTENT_PURPOSES)
  1468	    if purposes_fact is None or isinstance(purposes_fact, UnknownFact):
  1469	        # `evaluate_product` needs a concrete `purposes` set (spec §4.3:
  1470	        # `purposes=facts.require_known_set("intent.purposes")`) — with no
  1471	        # declared purpose at all, no per-product coverage test is even
  1472	        # meaningful, so we short-circuit here rather than run every
  1473	        # product's stage loop against an undefined purpose set.
  1474	        if global_review_reasons:
  1475	            return assemble(
  1476	                state=DecisionState.HUMAN_REVIEW_REQUIRED,
  1477	                review_reasons=global_review_reasons,
  1478	            )
  1479	        return assemble(state=DecisionState.NEEDS_INPUT, missing_facts=(FactPath.INTENT_PURPOSES,))
  1480	    purposes: frozenset[str] = frozenset(purposes_fact.value)  # type: ignore[union-attr]
  1481	
  1482	    products = sorted(
  1483	        (
  1484	            compiled_product
  1485	            for compiled_product in compiled_pack.products
  1486	            if compiled_product.product.status is VisaProductStatus.ACTIVE
  1487	            and _period_contains(compiled_product.product.valid_period, effective_at)
  1488	        ),
  1489	        key=lambda compiled_product: (
  1490	            compiled_product.product_code,
  1491	            str(compiled_product.product_version_id),
  1492	        ),
  1493	    )
  1494	
  1495	    proofs = [
  1496	        evaluate_product(
  1497	            product=compiled_product,
  1498	            rules=compiled_pack.rules_for(compiled_product, effective_at=effective_at),
  1499	            facts=snapshot,
  1500	            purposes=purposes,
  1501	            fact_registry=fact_registry,
  1502	            _trace_sink=trace_entries,
  1503	        )
  1504	        for compiled_product in products
  1505	    ]
  1506	
  1507	    # P0-B fix (gate round 1 item 2, see module docstring): REVIEW checked
  1508	    # before SUPPORTED — frozen precedence ranks HUMAN_REVIEW_REQUIRED above
  1509	    # SUPPORTED_CANDIDATES unconditionally, not only when the review trigger
  1510	    # happens to be GLOBAL (GLOBAL review triggers are handled first below).
  1511	    if global_review_reasons:
  1512	        return assemble(
  1513	            state=DecisionState.HUMAN_REVIEW_REQUIRED,
  1514	            review_reasons=global_review_reasons,
  1515	        )
  1516	
  1517	    review = [proof for proof in proofs if proof.status is ProductProofStatus.REVIEW]
  1518	    if review:
  1519	        review_reasons = _dedupe_reasons(reason for proof in review for reason in proof.reasons)
  1520	        return assemble(state=DecisionState.HUMAN_REVIEW_REQUIRED, review_reasons=review_reasons)
  1521	
  1522	    supported = [proof for proof in proofs if proof.status is ProductProofStatus.SUPPORTED]
  1523	    if supported:
  1524	        candidates = _rank_supported(
  1525	            supported,
  1526	            snapshot,
  1527	            compiled_pack,
  1528	            effective_at=effective_at,
  1529	            trace_sink=trace_entries,
  1530	        )
  1531	        return assemble(state=DecisionState.SUPPORTED_CANDIDATES, candidates=candidates)
  1532	
  1533	    blocked = [proof for proof in proofs if proof.status is ProductProofStatus.BLOCKED_UNKNOWN]
  1534	    if blocked:
  1535	        # P1 fix (gate round 1 item 6, see module docstring): the
  1536	        # deterministic MINIMAL viable set — the single BLOCKED_UNKNOWN
  1537	        # proof with the fewest missing_facts — rather than the union
  1538	        # across every blocked product. `min` ties break on first-seen
  1539	        # order, which is already the deterministic
  1540	        # (product_code, product_version_id) order `products`/`proofs` were
  1725	
  1726	    try:
  1727	        identity_provider = resolve_identity_provider()
  1728	        evaluation = evaluate_with_trace(
  1729	            facts,
  1730	            compiled,
  1731	            effective_at=now,
  1732	            observed_at=now,
  1733	            identity_provider=identity_provider,
  1734	        )
  1735	        decision = apply_public_policy_adapters(
  1736	            evaluation.decision,
  1737	            facts,
  1738	            compiled,
  1739	            disclosed_review_flags=disclosed_review_flags,
  1740	        )
  1741	        try:
  1742	            decision = _attach_price_quotes(
  1743	                decision,
  1744	                compiled,
  1745	                pricing_catalog=pricing_catalog,
  1746	            )
  1747	        except Exception as exc:
  1748	            logger.warning(
  1749	                "evaluate path: price quote projection failed: %s (trace=%s)",
  1750	                type(exc).__name__,
  1751	                request_trace,
  1752	            )
  1753	            pricing_catalog = UnavailablePricingCatalog()
  1754	        keyring = resolve_engine_hmac_keyring(compiled.environment, now)
  1755	        decision = seal_decision(
  1756	            decision,
  1757	            key=keyring.minting_key,
  1758	            trace=evaluation.trace,
  1759	        )
  1760	    except (PlaceholderIdentityNotAllowedError, FactsFingerprintKeyUnavailableError):
  1761	        logger.warning(
  1762	            "evaluate path: active pack environment=%s needs a real crypto "
  1763	            "identity_provider (STEP-6d) / a provisioned facts-fingerprint "
  1764	            "key, unavailable (trace=%s)",
  1765	            environment,
  1766	            request_trace,
  1767	        )
  1768	        return build_temp_unavailable_body(now=now, code="EVALUATION_UNAVAILABLE", mode=engine_mode)
  1769	    except FactsFingerprintKeyError:
  1770	        logger.warning(
  1771	            "evaluate path: malformed facts-fingerprint key config "
  1772	            "(VISA_ENGINE_FACTS_FINGERPRINT_KEYS_JSON), unavailable (trace=%s)",
  1773	            request_trace,
  1774	        )
  1775	        return build_temp_unavailable_body(now=now, code="EVALUATION_UNAVAILABLE", mode=engine_mode)
  1776	    except Exception as exc:  # defense-in-depth — evaluate() is documented pure/total
  1777	        # Log the exception TYPE only, never str(exc): evaluate() runs over
  1778	        # ApplicantFacts, and a stray ValidationError/KeyError message could
  1779	        # echo a raw fact value — this module must never log facts (Law 2).
  1780	        logger.warning("evaluate path: evaluate() failed: %s", type(exc).__name__)
  1781	        return build_temp_unavailable_body(now=now, code="EVALUATION_UNAVAILABLE", mode=engine_mode)
  1782	
  1783	    request_category = derive_request_category(facts, request_category_hint)
  1784	    # The request correlator IS the STEP-6d facts fingerprint (see module
  1785	    # docstring): keyed HMAC, non-reversible, exactly the G-a "distinct
  1786	    # requests" granularity.
  1787	    if decision.facts_fingerprint is None:  # pragma: no cover - evaluated-state invariant
  1788	        return build_temp_unavailable_body(now=now, code="EVALUATION_UNAVAILABLE", mode=engine_mode)
  1789	    request_fingerprint = bytes.fromhex(decision.facts_fingerprint.digest)
  1790

def _read_json(path: Path) -> dict[str, Any]:
    return json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))


def _canon(obj: Any) -> str:
    return json.dumps(obj, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"))


def _nodes(node: Any) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    out: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    if isinstance(node, dict):
        out.append(node)
        for value in node.values():
            out.extend(_nodes(value))
    elif isinstance(node, list):
        for value in node:
            out.extend(_nodes(value))
    return out


def _rules_by_id(payload: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, dict[str, Any]]:
    return {rule["rule_id"]: rule for rule in payload["rules"]}

    return out


def _decide(
    pack: compiler.CompiledRulePack, overrides: dict[str, Any], label: str
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """The applicant-facing outcome: the same verify-free compile → evaluate →
    ``apply_public_policy_adapters`` path ``gold_coverage_eval._evaluate``
    walks, with the pack handed in rather than selected from disk (the
    candidate is unsigned, so the selector cannot see it)."""
    persona = Persona(
        id=0, label=label, overrides=overrides, expected_state=DecisionState.NEEDS_INPUT
    )
    request = build_persona_request(persona)
    facts = request.applicant_facts()
    decision = evaluator.evaluate(
        facts,
        pack,
        effective_at=AS_OF,
        observed_at=AS_OF,
        identity_provider=_offline_identity_provider,
    )
    decision = evaluate_path.apply_public_policy_adapters(
        decision,
        facts,
        pack,
        disclosed_review_flags=request.effective_review_flags(),
    )
    return _decision_actual(decision)


def _replay(
    pack: compiler.CompiledRulePack, walks: dict[str, dict[str, Any]]
) -> dict[str, dict[str, Any]]:
    return {
        label: _decide(pack, spec["overrides"], label) for label, spec in sorted(walks.items())
    }
    }


def _known(value: Any) -> dict[str, Any]:
    return {"status": "KNOWN", "value": value}

class TestFoldIntegrity:
    def test_fold_is_deterministic_and_matches_disk(
        self,
        seq20_source: dict[str, Any],
        seq20_signed: dict[str, Any],
        seq21_source: dict[str, Any],
        prod_trust_store_env: None,
    ) -> None:
        assert fold(seq20_source, seq20_signed, observed_at=OBSERVED_AT) == seq21_source

    def test_fold_is_deterministic(
        self,
        seq20_source: dict[str, Any],
        seq20_signed: dict[str, Any],
        prod_trust_store_env: None,
    ) -> None:
        first = fold(seq20_source, seq20_signed, observed_at=OBSERVED_AT)
        second = fold(seq20_source, seq20_signed, observed_at=OBSERVED_AT)
        assert first == second

    def test_fold_refuses_without_a_trust_store(
        self,
        seq20_source: dict[str, Any],
        seq20_signed: dict[str, Any],
        monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch,
    ) -> None:
        """GUILT: the anchor must never be taken on the digest constant alone.
        Without the production PUBLIC key exported, the fold refuses instead
        of folding onto an unverified payload."""
        monkeypatch.delenv("VISA_ENGINE_TRUST_STORE_KEYS_JSON", raising=False)
        with pytest.raises(SystemExit) as excinfo:
            fold(seq20_source, seq20_signed, observed_at=OBSERVED_AT)
        assert "seq-20 anchor" in str(excinfo.value)

    def test_fold_refuses_a_base_pack_whose_review_rule_became_live(
        self, seq20_source: dict[str, Any]
    ) -> None:
        """GUILT: the nine retirements are justified by the rules being
        dormant (gated on a fact the browser never sets). A base pack that had
        given one of them a browser-reachable condition must abort the fold,
        not have its gate silently deleted.

        The pre-flight census is exercised DIRECTLY rather than through
        :func:`fold`: mutating the base pack also moves its JCS digest, so the
        chain-anchor check would abort first and this witness would prove that
        check instead of the one it names.
        """
        mutated = copy.deepcopy(seq20_source)
        for rule in mutated["rules"]:
            if rule["rule_id"] == "review.e33b.expertise-qualification":
                rule["required_facts"] = ["intent.purposes"]
                rule["when"] = {
                    "op": "intersects",
                    "fact": "intent.purposes",
                    "values": ["EMPLOYMENT"],
                }
        with pytest.raises(SystemExit) as excinfo:
            _assert_retired_review_rules_are_dormant(mutated)
        assert "intent.requested_product_code" in str(excinfo.value)

    def test_the_dormancy_census_passes_on_the_real_base_pack(
        self, seq20_source: dict[str, Any]
    ) -> None:
        """INNOCENCE for the guard above: it is not a check that always
        fails."""
        _assert_retired_review_rules_are_dormant(seq20_source)

    def test_fold_refuses_when_a_target_product_already_has_an_eligibility_rule(
        self,
        seq20_source: dict[str, Any],
        seq20_signed: dict[str, Any],
        seq21_source: dict[str, Any],
        prod_trust_store_env: None,
    ) -> None:
        """GUILT: folding seq-21 onto ITSELF (a pack that already carries the
        nine SUPPORT rules) must abort rather than add a second, unreconciled
        route to the same products."""
        with pytest.raises(SystemExit):
            fold(seq21_source, seq20_signed, observed_at=OBSERVED_AT)

    def test_compile_rule_pack_reports_ok(self) -> None:
        payload = load_rule_pack_payload(_SEQ21_SOURCE_PATH)
        report = compile_rule_pack(wrap_as_unsigned_pack(payload))
        assert report.ok, f"seq-21 does not compile clean: {report}"

    def test_source_validates_against_the_payload_model(
        self, seq21_source: dict[str, Any]
    ) -> None:
        assert RulePackPayload.model_validate(seq21_source).sequence == 21

class TestIdentity:
    def test_sequence_is_21(self, seq21_source: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
        assert seq21_source["sequence"] == 21

    def test_rule_pack_id_follows_the_uuid5_convention(
        self, seq21_source: dict[str, Any]
    ) -> None:
        assert seq21_source["rule_pack_id"] == str(_rule_pack_id(21))

    def test_chain_anchor_is_the_measured_seq20_digest(
        self, seq20_source: dict[str, Any], seq21_source: dict[str, Any]
    ) -> None:
        """The anchor is re-derived from the seq-20 bytes on disk, never taken
        from the constant alone."""
        recomputed = hashlib.sha256(canonicalize_json(seq20_source)).hexdigest()
        assert recomputed == SEQ20_PAYLOAD_SHA256
        assert seq21_source["previous_payload_sha256"] == SEQ20_PAYLOAD_SHA256

    def test_chain_anchor_is_also_the_signed_artifacts_own_digest(
        self, seq20_signed: dict[str, Any]
    ) -> None:
        assert seq20_signed["payload_sha256"] == SEQ20_PAYLOAD_SHA256

    def test_payload_digest_survives_reformatting_of_the_file(
        self, seq21_source: dict[str, Any]
    ) -> None:
        """The pack's identity is JCS over the PARSED document, never the file
        bytes, so the repo's prettier gate can reshape the file freely. The
        constant is the digest the owner signs; it was measured BEFORE the
        prettier pass and re-measured after it, unchanged."""
        digest = hashlib.sha256(canonicalize_json(seq21_source)).hexdigest()
        assert digest == SEQ21_PAYLOAD_SHA256

    def test_validity_opens_after_the_expected_signature(
        self, seq21_source: dict[str, Any], seq20_source: dict[str, Any]
    ) -> None:
        """seq-21's window opens on a FUTURE date, not on the fold date.

        A candidate whose ``valid_period.from`` is already in the past is a
        retroactive legal claim, and it is also what made the first seq-21
        census report "0 walks moved": the replay ran at an instant before the
        rules were in force. Opening after the expected signature makes every
        replay in this module reproducible by a third party at any instant
        inside the window.
        """
        assert seq21_source["valid_period"] == {"to": None, "from": PACK_VALID_FROM}
        opens = datetime.fromisoformat(PACK_VALID_FROM.replace("Z", "+00:00"))
        assert opens > datetime.fromisoformat(
            seq21_source["created_at"].replace("Z", "+00:00")
        )
        assert opens > datetime.fromisoformat(
            seq20_source["valid_period"]["from"].replace("Z", "+00:00")
        )
        assert AS_OF >= opens

    def test_rollback_of_payload_sha256_is_null(self, seq21_source: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
        assert seq21_source["rollback_of_payload_sha256"] is None

    def test_products_and_sources_are_untouched(
        self, seq20_source: dict[str, Any], seq21_source: dict[str, Any]
    ) -> None:
        for key in (
            "environment",
            "jurisdiction",
            "decision_domain",
            "hit_policy",
            "products",
            "source_records",
            "engine_min_version",
            "engine_max_version",
            "engine_contract_version",
        ):
            assert _canon(seq21_source[key]) == _canon(seq20_source[key]), key

class TestRetiredReviewRules:
    def test_every_retired_rule_was_dormant_in_seq20(
        self, seq20_source: dict[str, Any]
    ) -> None:
        """INNOCENCE: nothing live was deleted. Each retired rule is a
        REQUIRE_REVIEW rule gated on ``intent.requested_product_code`` — the
        fact ``fact-mapper.ts`` hard-codes to UNKNOWN(NOT_ASKED), so no browser
        answer could ever make it fire."""
        rules = _rules_by_id(seq20_source)
        for rule_id in RETIRED_REVIEW_RULES:
            rule = rules[rule_id]
            assert rule["effect"]["type"] == "REQUIRE_REVIEW", rule_id
            assert "intent.requested_product_code" in rule["required_facts"], rule_id

    def test_retired_rules_are_absent_from_seq21(self, seq21_source: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
        present = sorted(set(RETIRED_REVIEW_RULES) & set(_rules_by_id(seq21_source)))
        assert present == []

    def test_no_review_rule_survives_on_requested_product_code_for_a_target_product(
        self, seq21_source: dict[str, Any]
    ) -> None:
        """GUILT for A4: a REQUIRE_REVIEW rule that is UNKNOWN on
        ``intent.requested_product_code`` makes its product BLOCKED_UNKNOWN
        BEFORE ``purposes <= covered`` is ever tested
        (``evaluator.evaluate_product``), so one left behind would make the
        nine new SUPPORT rules structurally unable to produce a candidate."""
        products = {
            product["product_code"]: product["product_version_id"]
            for product in seq21_source["products"]
        }
        targets = {products[code] for code in TARGET_PRODUCT_CODES}
        offenders = [
            rule["rule_id"]
            for rule in seq21_source["rules"]
            if rule["stage"] == "HUMAN_REVIEW"
            and rule["on_unknown"] != "NO_EFFECT"
            and "intent.requested_product_code" in rule["required_facts"]
            and targets & set(rule["product_version_ids"])
        ]
        assert offenders == []

    def test_no_retired_rule_was_flipped_to_no_effect_instead(
        self, seq21_source: dict[str, Any]
    ) -> None:
        """The dossier's §4 fail-open, stated as a test: a REQUIRE_REVIEW rule
        made ``NO_EFFECT`` still claims to police a qualification while being
        unable to block anything. None of the nine is in the pack at all."""
        for rule_id in RETIRED_REVIEW_RULES:
            assert rule_id not in _rules_by_id(seq21_source)

    def test_no_other_rule_moved(
        self, seq20_source: dict[str, Any], seq21_source: dict[str, Any]
    ) -> None:
        before = _rules_by_id(seq20_source)
        after = _rules_by_id(seq21_source)
        assert set(before) - set(after) == set(RETIRED_REVIEW_RULES)
        assert set(after) - set(before) == set(NEW_RULE_IDS)
        for rule_id, rule in after.items():
            if rule_id in set(NEW_RULE_IDS):
                continue
            assert _canon(rule) == _canon(before[rule_id]), rule_id

class TestSupportRuleShape:
    def test_every_target_product_has_exactly_one_eligibility_rule(
        self, seq21_source: dict[str, Any]
    ) -> None:
        products = {
            product["product_code"]: product["product_version_id"]
            for product in seq21_source["products"]
        }
        for row in SUPPORT_RULES:
            version_id = products[row["product_code"]]
            ids = sorted(
                rule["rule_id"]
                for rule in seq21_source["rules"]
                if rule["stage"] == "ELIGIBILITY" and version_id in rule["product_version_ids"]
            )
            assert ids == [row["rule_id"]], row["product_code"]
"""Unit tests for the reachability_report CLI (QW-3).

Ground-truth strategy: several assertions here re-derive an expected value
with an INDEPENDENT code path (a raw-JSON recursive walk, not
``ast.collect_fact_paths``/``rule.required_facts``) rather than mirroring the
production module's own logic — a test that reimplements the function under
test in slightly different words and calls that "verification" only proves
self-consistency, not correctness (cicatrix family #6). Where an independent
re-derivation isn't practical (e.g. the pydantic-model-level orphan check),
the test instead exercises guilt AND innocence on a small synthetic pack
(cicatrix family #3's guard-conformance discipline: no check ships without
both).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import copy
import json
import re
import uuid
from pathlib import Path

import pytest
from pydantic import ValidationError

from backend.scripts.visa_engine.reachability_report import (
    DEFAULT_FACT_MAPPER_PATH,
    build_report,
    main,
    report_to_json,
    report_to_markdown,
)
from backend.services.visa_engine.fact_registry import DEFAULT_FACT_REGISTRY

PACKS_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[4] / "backend/services/visa_engine/contracts/packs"
SEQ7_PACK = PACKS_DIR / "rulepack-prod-007.source.json"
SEQ6_PACK = PACKS_DIR / "rulepack-prod-006.source.json"

# The exact unreachable set pinned by
# test_seq6_refuter_witnesses.py::test_reachability_is_what_the_document_claims
# for seq-6. This module's own report on seq-7 must reproduce it (seq-7 made
# no reachability-affecting change to that set — a real drift is exactly what
# this pin exists to catch).
PINNED_UNREACHABLE_CODES = [
    "E23U",
    "E23V",
    "E28B",
    "E28C",
    "E28D",
    "E28F",
    "E30E",
    "E30F",
    "E33A",
    "E33B",
    "E33C",
]


def _independent_fact_walk(when: dict) -> set[str]:
    """Ground truth for "which facts does this condition tree reference",
    written independently of ``ast.collect_fact_paths`` / ``required_facts``
    — a raw recursive walk of the JSON condition tree."""
    out: set[str] = set()

    def walk(node: object) -> None:
        if isinstance(node, dict):
            fact = node.get("fact")
            if fact is not None:
                out.add(fact)
            for key, value in node.items():
                if key != "fact":
                    walk(value)
        elif isinstance(node, list):
            for item in node:
                walk(item)

    walk(when)
    return out


@pytest.fixture(scope="module")
def seq7_raw() -> dict:
    return json.loads(SEQ7_PACK.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))


@pytest.fixture(scope="module")
def seq7_report():
    return build_report(SEQ7_PACK)


def test_seq7_pack_exists_and_is_sequence_7(seq7_raw: dict) -> None:
    """Anti-hallucination anchor (CLAUDE.md §6): assert the fixture this
    whole file leans on really is what every other assertion assumes."""
    assert seq7_raw["sequence"] == 7


def test_seq6_pack_reproduces_its_own_pinned_assertion() -> None:
    """Sanity check on the tool itself, independent of seq-7: run it against
    seq-6 and confirm it reproduces exactly what
    test_seq6_refuter_witnesses.py::test_reachability_is_what_the_document_claims
    already asserts by hand against that same file. If this ever disagrees
    with that test, the bug is in THIS script, not in seq-6."""
    report = build_report(SEQ6_PACK)
    assert len(report.reachable_product_codes) == 27
    assert list(report.blocked_product_codes) == PINNED_UNREACHABLE_CODES


def test_reachability_matches_the_seq6_pin(seq7_report) -> None:
    """The headline number the task brief asks for: does seq-7 diverge from
    the seq-6 split pinned in test_seq6_refuter_witnesses.py? Answer: no."""
    assert len(seq7_report.reachable_product_codes) == 27
    assert len(seq7_report.blocked_product_codes) == 11
    assert list(seq7_report.blocked_product_codes) == PINNED_UNREACHABLE_CODES
    assert (set(seq7_report.reachable_product_codes) | set(seq7_report.blocked_product_codes)) == {
        p.product_code for p in seq7_report.products
    }


def test_reachable_and_blocked_partition_all_products(seq7_report) -> None:
    reachable = set(seq7_report.reachable_product_codes)
    blocked = set(seq7_report.blocked_product_codes)
    assert reachable & blocked == set()
    assert len(reachable) + len(blocked) == seq7_report.product_count


def test_fact_path_usage_matches_independent_walk(seq7_raw: dict) -> None:
    used_by_independent_walk: set[str] = set()
    for rule in seq7_raw["rules"]:
        used_by_independent_walk |= _independent_fact_walk(rule["when"])

    report = build_report(SEQ7_PACK)
    assert set(report.used_fact_paths) == used_by_independent_walk


def test_unused_fact_paths_is_registry_minus_used(seq7_report) -> None:
    all_paths = {str(p.value) for p in DEFAULT_FACT_REGISTRY.all_paths()}
    assert set(seq7_report.unused_fact_paths) == all_paths - set(seq7_report.used_fact_paths)
    assert seq7_report.total_fact_paths == len(all_paths)
    # The exact 14-path headline (was 8; 2026-08-23 vocabulary extension —
    # PR #4650 — added 4 new registry paths that no rule in
    # rulepack-prod-007.source.json references yet, which is exactly what
    # "vocabulary-only, no rulepack change" means: `derived.has_active_stay_permit`,
    # `family.sponsor_permit_basis`, `family.stepchild_marriage_certificate_confirmed`,
    # `family.stepchild_birth_certificate_confirmed`). Was 12; 2026-08-24 F4
    # (D12 active-stay-permit exclusion) adds the 13th, `immigration.renewal_paid` —
    # also vocabulary-only against this frozen seq-7 baseline. Was 13; PR-D4c-1
    # adds the 14th, `investment.investment_amount_usd` — again vocabulary-only:
    # this frozen seq-7 pack has no rule that reads it. This is not a counter
    # update, it is the receipt — the count rising by exactly one is what
    # "declared but read by no rule" looks like from the reachability report's
    # side, and it is this PR's central claim. Unlike the other four, it stays
    # unused *by design* until a future seq folds a rule that reads it: a
    # deliberately dormant fact, not an accidentally orphaned one — do not
    # "fix" it by bumping the number down.
    #
    # Was 14; W-VO-S21 (2026-09-13) adds the TEN seq-21 qualification
    # booleans, taking it to 24. The same receipt reading applies with one
    # difference worth stating: unlike `investment.investment_amount_usd`,
    # these ten ARE read by rules — but by rules that live in
    # `rulepack-prod-021.source.json`, and this fixture is pinned to the
    # FROZEN seq-7 pack. "Unused against seq-7" is therefore the expected
    # reading of a fact introduced fourteen sequences later, and the number
    # rising by exactly ten is the receipt that the registry grew by exactly
    # ten. `test_seq21_pack.py` is where those rules' readers are proven.
    assert len(seq7_report.unused_fact_paths) == 24

def test_not_asked_facts_are_exactly_the_five_hardcoded_in_the_mapper() -> None:
    assert DEFAULT_FACT_MAPPER_PATH.exists(), (
        "the default fact-mapper path is stale — the live interview moved "
        "and this script's default needs updating"
    )
    text = DEFAULT_FACT_MAPPER_PATH.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    # Independent extraction: a plain unconditional-assignment regex, not the
    # module's own compiled pattern.
    found = sorted(set(re.findall(r'"([a-z_]+\.[a-z_]+)":\s*unknownFact\(NOT_ASKED\),', text)))
    # `immigration.renewal_paid` used to be a sixth entry here, but 2026-08-24
    # F4 (D12 active-stay-permit exclusion) shipped the real interview
    # question for it (tree.ts, gated in flow.ts's
    # `computeNextNode`/`shouldAskRenewalPaid`), so fact-mapper.ts:591 now
    # maps it through `booleanFact(facts.renewal_paid)` — a real answered
    # fact, not an unconditional NOT_ASKED placeholder. It correctly dropped
    # out of this list. PR-D4c-1 (2026-09-13) put a NEW sixth entry back in:
    # `investment.investment_amount_usd` was contract-only (the wire key
    # existed for a later PR, D4c-2, to send an answer through), so
    # fact-mapper.ts mapped it through the same unconditional
    # `unknownFact(NOT_ASKED)` idiom every other not-yet-interviewed fact
    # uses. PR-D4c-2 (THIS PR, 2026-09-13) is that later PR: the
    # `merit`/`family`/`undecided` investment-vehicle branches now ask a real
    # currency-bound question for it (`investment_currency`/
    # `investment_amount_usd`, tree.ts, gated in flow.ts's
    # `getCategoryQuestionIds`), so fact-mapper.ts now maps it through
    # `integerFact(facts.investment_amount_usd, ...)` — a real, conditionally
    # answered fact (KNOWN when `usd` was chosen and answered, an explicit
    # UNKNOWN otherwise), never an unconditional NOT_ASKED placeholder. It
    # correctly drops out of this list, the same way `immigration.
    # renewal_paid` did before it — six back to five.
    assert found == [
        "commercial.service_fee_budget_idr",
        "commercial.wants_quote",
        "immigration.last_entry_date",
        "intent.desired_entry_date",
        "intent.requested_product_code",
    ]

    report = build_report(SEQ7_PACK)
    assert list(report.not_asked_facts) == found

   605	class TestSupportRuleShape:
   606	    def test_every_target_product_has_exactly_one_eligibility_rule(
   607	        self, seq21_source: dict[str, Any]
   608	    ) -> None:
   609	        products = {
   610	            product["product_code"]: product["product_version_id"]
   611	            for product in seq21_source["products"]
   612	        }
   613	        for row in SUPPORT_RULES:
   614	            version_id = products[row["product_code"]]
   615	            ids = sorted(
   616	                rule["rule_id"]
   617	                for rule in seq21_source["rules"]
   618	                if rule["stage"] == "ELIGIBILITY" and version_id in rule["product_version_ids"]
   619	            )
   620	            assert ids == [row["rule_id"]], row["product_code"]
   621	
   622	    def test_every_support_rule_reads_its_own_qualifying_fact(
   623	        self, seq21_source: dict[str, Any]
   624	    ) -> None:
   625	        """The cure, stated positively: no SUPPORT rule here is keyed on
   626	        ``sponsor.type`` (or a route) alone."""
   627	        rules = _rules_by_id(seq21_source)
   628	        for row in SUPPORT_RULES:
   629	            rule = rules[row["rule_id"]]
   630	            assert row["qualifying_fact"] in QUALIFICATION_FACTS
   631	            assert row["qualifying_fact"] in rule["required_facts"], row["rule_id"]
   632	            eq_nodes = [
   633	                node
   634	                for node in _nodes(rule["when"])
   635	                if node.get("fact") == row["qualifying_fact"]
   636	                and node.get("op") == "eq"
   637	                and node.get("value") is True
   638	            ]
   639	            assert len(eq_nodes) == 1, row["rule_id"]
   640	
   641	    def test_no_two_support_rules_share_a_condition(
   642	        self, seq21_source: dict[str, Any]
   643	    ) -> None:
   644	        """GUILT, and the precise defect PR #6362 shipped: ``el.e33a``,
   645	        ``el.e33b`` and ``el.e23v`` there had one byte-identical ``when``, so a
   646	        single answer produced three products no fact distinguished."""
   647	        rules = _rules_by_id(seq21_source)
   648	        conditions = [_canon(rules[row["rule_id"]]["when"]) for row in SUPPORT_RULES]
   649	        duplicates = [item for item, count in Counter(conditions).items() if count > 1]
   650	        assert duplicates == []

   652	    def test_every_support_rule_asks_rather_than_denies_on_an_unknown_qualification(

   662	        assert QUALIFICATION_FACTS <= {path.value for path in DEFAULT_FACT_REGISTRY.all_paths()}

   664	    def test_support_purposes_are_covered_by_the_product_catalogue(
   665	        self, seq21_source: dict[str, Any]
   666	    ) -> None:

   673	    def test_no_e28_rule_invents_a_usd_figure(self, seq21_source: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
   674	        """No source record in this pack states a Golden Visa USD minimum, so
   675	        the four E28 rules must depend on the DECLARED
   676	        ``investment.meets_published_threshold`` and never on a hard-coded
   677	        comparison against ``investment.investment_amount_usd``."""
   678	        rules = _rules_by_id(seq21_source)

   683	            assert "investment.meets_published_threshold" in rule["required_facts"]

   685	            assert rule["source_refs"], row["rule_id"]

   693	class TestNamedCauseRules:
   694	    def test_e33_guarantee_rule_mirrors_the_packs_own_bounds(
   695	        self, seq21_source: dict[str, Any]
   696	    ) -> None:
   697	        """The EXCLUDE's bounds are the SUPPORT rules' bounds, read from the
   698	        pack — a second copy of the number would be free to drift, and the
   699	        pack would then deny below X while granting at Y."""
   700	        rules = _rules_by_id(seq21_source)
   701	        rule = rules[E33_GUARANTEE_RULE_ID]
   702	        deposit_support = [
   703	            node
   704	            for node in _nodes(rules["el.e33.deposit-basis"]["when"])
   705	            if node.get("fact") == "secondhome.bank_deposit_usd" and node.get("op") == "gte"
   706	        ]
   707	        property_support = [
   708	            node
   709	            for node in _nodes(rules["el.e33.property-basis"]["when"])
   710	            if node.get("fact") == "secondhome.qualifying_property_value_usd"
   711	            and node.get("op") == "gte"
   712	        ]
   713	        exclude = {
   714	            node["fact"]: node["value"]
   715	            for node in _nodes(rule["when"])
   716	            if node.get("op") == "lt"
   717	        }
   718	        assert exclude["secondhome.bank_deposit_usd"] == deposit_support[0]["value"]
   719	        assert (
   720	            exclude["secondhome.qualifying_property_value_usd"] == property_support[0]["value"]
   721	        )

   761	class TestTheNineProductsAreReachable:
   762	    def test_each_target_product_is_supported_on_its_gold_fixture(
   763	        self,
   764	        seq21_compiled: compiler.CompiledRulePack,
   765	        gold_base: dict[str, Any],
   766	    ) -> None:
   767	        """The objective, measured: all nine of the products with no SUPPORT
   768	        rule on seq-20 are named by the engine on facts the interview can ask."""
   769	        missing: list[str] = []
   770	        for code, override in _gold_overrides().items():
   771	            facts = {**gold_base, **override}
   772	            actual = _decide(seq21_compiled, facts, f"gold/{code}")
   773	            if actual["state"] != "SUPPORTED_CANDIDATES" or code not in actual["candidates"]:
   774	                missing.append(f"{code}: {actual['state']} {actual['candidates']}")
   775	        assert missing == []

   777	    def test_seq20_reaches_none_of_them_on_the_same_fixtures(
   778	        self,
   779	        seq20_compiled: compiler.CompiledRulePack,
   780	        gold_base: dict[str, Any],
   781	    ) -> None:
   782	        """INNOCENCE for the claim that this fold is what moved them: the SAME
   783	        nine fact bags against the signed-today pack name none of the nine."""
   784	        reached = []
   785	        for code, override in _gold_overrides().items():
   786	            facts = {**gold_base, **override}
   787	            actual = _decide(seq20_compiled, facts, f"gold/{code}")
   788	            if code in actual["candidates"]:
   789	                reached.append(code)
   790	        assert reached == []

   792	    def test_an_unknown_qualification_asks_instead_of_supporting(
   793	        self,
   794	        seq21_compiled: compiler.CompiledRulePack,
   795	        gold_base: dict[str, Any],
   796	    ) -> None:
   797	        """GUILT: withdraw the qualifying fact from each gold fixture and the
   798	        product must disappear from the candidates, with the outcome becoming
   799	        a QUESTION (``NEEDS_INPUT``) rather than a silent denial or, worse, a
   800	        SUPPORT on the sponsor category alone."""
   801	        offenders: list[str] = []
   802	        for code, override in _gold_overrides().items():
   803	            stripped = {
   804	                key: (_UNKNOWN if key in QUALIFICATION_FACTS else value)
   805	                for key, value in override.items()
   806	            }
   807	            actual = _decide(seq21_compiled, {**gold_base, **stripped}, f"gold-unknown/{code}")
   808	            if code in actual["candidates"] or actual["state"] != "NEEDS_INPUT":
   809	                offenders.append(f"{code}: {actual['state']} {actual['candidates']}")
   810	        assert offenders == []

   814	# Behaviour — the guilt witness for the cure itself
   815	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

   817	
   818	class TestSponsorTypeAloneIsNotEvidence:
   819	    """Re-inject the defect and prove the corpus notices.
   820	
   821	    ``_uncured`` removes ONLY the qualifying-fact conjunct from the nine
   822	    SUPPORT rules, which is exactly the shape PR #6362 shipped for its five.
   823	    If the census does not move, the qualifying facts are decorative and this
   824	    whole fold is theatre.
   825	    """
   826	
   827	    @staticmethod
   828	    def _uncured(seq21_source: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
   829	        mutated = copy.deepcopy(seq21_source)
   830	        quals = {row["rule_id"]: row["qualifying_fact"] for row in SUPPORT_RULES}
   831	        for rule in mutated["rules"]:
   832	            fact = quals.get(rule["rule_id"])
   833	            if fact is None:
   834	                continue
   835	            rule["when"]["args"] = [
   836	                arg for arg in rule["when"]["args"] if arg.get("fact") != fact
   837	            ]
   838	            rule["required_facts"] = sorted(
   839	                path for path in rule["required_facts"] if path != fact
   840	            )
   841	        return mutated
   842	
   843	    def test_stripping_the_qualification_hands_products_out_on_no_evidence(
   844	        self,
   845	        seq21_source: dict[str, Any],
   846	        seq21_compiled: compiler.CompiledRulePack,
   847	        walks: dict[str, dict[str, Any]],
   848	    ) -> None:
   849	        cured = _replay(seq21_compiled, walks)
   850	        uncured = _replay(_compiled(self._uncured(seq21_source)), walks)
   851	        moved = [label for label in cured if cured[label] != uncured[label]]
   852	        assert len(moved) >= 16, (
   853	            "removing the qualifying facts moved only "
   854	            f"{len(moved)} walks — the conjuncts are not load-bearing"
   855	        )
   856	
   857	    def test_a_sponsor_type_of_none_would_gain_e33b(
   858	        self,
   859	        seq21_source: dict[str, Any],
   860	        seq21_compiled: compiler.CompiledRulePack,
   861	        walks: dict[str, dict[str, Any]],
   862	    ) -> None:
   863	        """The named guilt: ``offshore/work`` and ``offshore/other`` both
   864	        declare ``sponsor.type = NONE``. Un-cured, the pack offers them E33B
   865	        with nothing having established a collaboration."""
   866	        label = "offshore/work"
   867	        cured = _decide(seq21_compiled, walks[label]["overrides"], label)
   868	        uncured = _decide(
   869	            _compiled(self._uncured(seq21_source)), walks[label]["overrides"], label
   870	        )
   871	        assert "E33B" not in cured["candidates"]
   872	        assert "E33B" in uncured["candidates"]
   873	
   874	    def test_a_government_sponsor_would_gain_three_products_at_once(
   875	        self,
   876	        seq21_source: dict[str, Any],
   877	        seq21_compiled: compiler.CompiledRulePack,
   878	        walks: dict[str, dict[str, Any]],
   879	    ) -> None:
   880	        """The dossier's §4 finding, reproduced: un-cured, ONE answer produces
   881	        E23V + E33A + E33B together because nothing tells them apart."""
   882	        label = "offshore/work/sponsor_government"
   883	        cured = _decide(seq21_compiled, walks[label]["overrides"], label)
   884	        uncured = _decide(
   885	            _compiled(self._uncured(seq21_source)), walks[label]["overrides"], label
   886	        )
   887	        assert cured["candidates"] == ["E23"]
   888	        assert {"E23V", "E33A", "E33B"} <= set(uncured["candidates"])

   896	class TestCensusReplay:
   897	    def test_no_walk_changes_state_or_candidates(
   898	        self,
   899	        seq20_compiled: compiler.CompiledRulePack,
   900	        seq21_compiled: compiler.CompiledRulePack,
   901	        walks: dict[str, dict[str, Any]],
   902	    ) -> None:
   903	        """The honest measurement, and it is a NEGATIVE one: the corpus does
   904	        not yet carry the ten new facts (W-VO-Q adds the questions), so no walk
   905	        gains a product. What must NOT happen is a regression — a walk losing
   906	        its answer, or an ``on_unknown: NEEDS_INPUT`` rule turning a decided
   907	        dead end into a question."""
   908	        before = _replay(seq20_compiled, walks)
   909	        after = _replay(seq21_compiled, walks)
   910	        drift = [
   911	            f"{label}: {before[label]['state']} {before[label]['candidates']} -> "
   912	            f"{after[label]['state']} {after[label]['candidates']}"
   913	            for label in sorted(before)
   914	            if (before[label]["state"], before[label]["candidates"])
   915	            != (after[label]["state"], after[label]["candidates"])
   916	        ]
   917	        assert drift == []
   918	
   919	    def test_the_census_is_still_67_answers_15_no_paths_2_questions(
   920	        self,
   920	        self,
   921	        seq21_compiled: compiler.CompiledRulePack,
   922	        walks: dict[str, dict[str, Any]],
   923	    ) -> None:
   924	        census = Counter(actual["state"] for actual in _replay(seq21_compiled, walks).values())
   925	        assert census["SUPPORTED_CANDIDATES"] == 67
   926	        assert census["NO_SUPPORTED_PATH"] == 15
   927	        assert census["NEEDS_INPUT"] == 2
   928	        assert census["HUMAN_REVIEW_REQUIRED"] == 0
   929	
   930	    def test_no_walk_regresses_onto_requested_product_code(
   931	        self,
   932	        seq21_compiled: compiler.CompiledRulePack,
   933	        walks: dict[str, dict[str, Any]],
   934	    ) -> None:
   935	        """A4. ``intent.requested_product_code`` is never asked by the browser,
   936	        so a walk blocked on it is a question the funnel cannot honour."""
   937	        offenders = [
   938	            label
   939	            for label, actual in _replay(seq21_compiled, walks).items()
   940	            if "intent.requested_product_code" in actual["missing_facts"]
   941	        ]
   942	        assert offenders == []
   943	
   944	    def test_the_three_generic_dead_ends_now_name_their_cause(
   945	        self,
   946	        seq20_compiled: compiler.CompiledRulePack,
   947	        seq21_compiled: compiler.CompiledRulePack,
   948	        walks: dict[str, dict[str, Any]],
   949	    ) -> None:
   950	        before = _replay(seq20_compiled, walks)
   951	        after = _replay(seq21_compiled, walks)
   952	        for label, expected_code in NAMED_CAUSE_WALKS.items():
   953	            assert before[label]["no_path_reason_codes"] == [_GENERIC_CAUSE], label
   954	            codes = after[label]["no_path_reason_codes"]

"""Replay the 20 canonical Visa Oracle gold personas against a real RulePack.

This is the missing G-b evidence driver.  Unlike the older fixture replay in
``backend.tests.services.visa_engine.gold_replay``, both modes exercise policy
that can be compared with production:

* ``--live`` posts every canonical persona to the public evaluate endpoint as
  ``traffic_source=synthetic_gold``.  The driver token is read only from the
  operator-owned token file; it has no CLI option and is never logged.
* ``--offline`` verifies, compiles, and evaluates the highest-sequence signed
  PRODUCTION pack actually present in ``contracts/packs``.  It then calls the
  same deterministic, no-I/O policy adapter helper as the public evaluate path.
  This proves only what that repository artifact and those checked-out policy
  adapters do; it never claims that the artifact is the active production pack.
  Offline mode runs inside the repository's backend environment and therefore
  requires the serving stack's lock-pinned dependencies; it is not a standalone
  stdlib utility.

The JSON report keeps every divergence visible.  By default every divergent
persona has ``"explanation": null`` and therefore makes the command exit 1.
After an independent reviewer fills those fields in a saved report, pass that
report back with ``--accepted-explanations``.  Explained divergences remain
catalogued as divergences, but no longer count as *unexplained* for G-b's exit
criterion.

Usage::

    cd apps/backend-rag && source .venv/bin/activate
    PYTHONPATH=. python -m backend.scripts.visa_engine.gold_replay_driver \
      --offline --out /tmp/visa-gold-replay-offline.json

    PYTHONPATH=. python -m backend.scripts.visa_engine.gold_replay_driver \
      --live --out /tmp/visa-gold-replay-live.json
"""

class GoldReplayDriverError(RuntimeError):
    """Operational failure that prevents a complete, trustworthy report."""


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class AcceptedExplanation:
    """A reviewed explanation bound to the exact divergence it accepted."""

    explanation: str
    expected: Mapping[str, Any]
    actual: Mapping[str, Any]
    pack: Mapping[str, Any]

def _offline_identity_provider(
    facts: ApplicantFacts,
    rule_pack_ref: RulePackRef,
    effective_at: datetime,
    _environment: Environment,
) -> DecisionIdentity:
    """Build deterministic offline-only identities for a PRODUCTION pack.

    The evaluator correctly refuses its TEST placeholder for a PRODUCTION
    RulePack.  This explicitly injected provider uses a named non-secret key
    solely to let the pure local evaluator construct its required Decision
    identity.  Identity/fingerprint values are intentionally omitted from the
    report and must never be represented as production integrity evidence.
    """

    return build_decision_identity(
        facts,
        rule_pack_ref,
        effective_at,
        fingerprint_key=b"visa-gold-replay-offline-non-secret-v1",
        fingerprint_key_id="gold-replay-offline-non-secret-v1",
    )


def _parse_utc(value: str) -> datetime:
    parsed = datetime.fromisoformat(value.replace("Z", "+00:00"))
    if parsed.tzinfo is None or parsed.utcoffset() != timezone.utc.utcoffset(parsed):
        raise ValueError(f"timestamp must be timezone-aware UTC: {value!r}")
    return parsed


def _decode_public_key(value: str) -> Ed25519PublicKey:
    raw = base64.urlsafe_b64decode(value + "=" * (-len(value) % 4))
    if len(raw) != 32:
        raise GoldReplayDriverError("repository trust key is not a 32-byte Ed25519 key")
    return Ed25519PublicKey.from_public_bytes(raw)


def _repository_trust_store() -> StaticTrustStore:
    keys = []
    for entry in _REPOSITORY_PRODUCTION_SIGNING_KEYS:
        valid_to = entry["valid_to"]
        revoked_at = entry["revoked_at"]
        keys.append(
            TrustedSigningKey(
                key_id=str(entry["kid"]),
                public_key=_decode_public_key(str(entry["public_key"])),
                valid_from=_parse_utc(str(entry["valid_from"])),
                valid_to=None if valid_to is None else _parse_utc(valid_to),
                revoked_at=None if revoked_at is None else _parse_utc(revoked_at),
                environment=str(entry["environment"]),
            )
        )
    return StaticTrustStore(keys)

  1145	      // judgment on an uncertain exclusion outranks merely asking the

   465	def _assert_retired_review_rules_are_dormant(payload: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
   466	    """Every rule this fold retires must be a REQUIRE_REVIEW rule gated on
   467	    ``intent.requested_product_code``, scoped to the product it is declared
   468	    against.
   469	
   470	    The retirement's justification is that the rule is dormant BY
   471	    CONSTRUCTION (``fact-mapper.ts`` never sets that fact) and that its review
   472	    question is now a fact the new SUPPORT rule tests. If a future base pack
   473	    gives one of them a condition that can actually fire from the browser,
   474	    retiring it would drop a live gate — so this refuses rather than deleting.
   475	    """
   476	    rules_by_id = _rules_by_id(payload)
   477	    products = _products_by_code(payload)
   478	    for rule_id, product_code in RETIRED_REVIEW_RULES.items():
   479	        rule = rules_by_id.get(rule_id)
   480	        if rule is None:
   481	            _fail(f"rule {rule_id!r} is not in the base pack — the edit set is stale")
   482	        if rule["effect"]["type"] != "REQUIRE_REVIEW":
   483	            _fail(
   484	                f"{rule_id!r} is a {rule['effect']['type']} rule, not REQUIRE_REVIEW — "
   485	                "refusing to retire it under an edit that only claims to retire "
   486	                "dormant review gates"
   487	            )
   488	        if REQUESTED_PRODUCT_FACT not in (rule.get("required_facts") or []):
   489	            _fail(
   490	                f"{rule_id!r} no longer reads {REQUESTED_PRODUCT_FACT} — it can now "
   491	                "fire from the browser, so retiring it would drop a live gate"
   492	            )
   493	        version_id = products[product_code]["product_version_id"]
   494	        if version_id not in rule.get("product_version_ids", []):
   495	            _fail(
   496	                f"{rule_id!r} is not scoped to {product_code} — the declared "
   497	                "rule/product pairing is stale"
   498	            )

   500	
   501	def _bound_nodes(rule: dict[str, Any], fact: str, op: str) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
   502	    return [
   503	        node for node in _nodes(rule.get("when")) if node.get("fact") == fact and node.get("op") == op
   504	    ]

   507	def _e33_guarantee_bounds(payload: dict[str, Any]) -> tuple[int, int]:
   508	    """``(deposit_usd_minimum, property_usd_minimum)``, READ from the two E33
   509	    SUPPORT rules that already encode them.
   510	
   511	    The named-cause EXCLUDE this fold adds says "below the threshold". If the
   512	    number it uses were typed here it could drift from the number the SUPPORT
   513	    rule uses, and the pack would simultaneously deny a product for being
   514	    below X and grant it at Y. Extracting both makes that impossible and turns
   515	    a moved bound into a fold abort.
   516	    """
   517	    rules_by_id = _rules_by_id(payload)
   518	    bounds: list[int] = []
   519	    for rule_id, fact in (
   520	        (E33_DEPOSIT_DONOR_RULE_ID, DEPOSIT_FACT),
   521	        (E33_PROPERTY_DONOR_RULE_ID, PROPERTY_FACT),
   522	    ):
   523	        rule = rules_by_id.get(rule_id)
   524	        if rule is None:
   525	            _fail(f"rule {rule_id!r} is missing — cannot derive the E33 guarantee bound")
   526	        nodes = _bound_nodes(rule, fact, "gte")
   527	        if len(nodes) != 1:
   528	            _fail(
   529	                f"rule {rule_id!r} carries {len(nodes)} '{fact} gte' bounds; exactly "
   530	                "one is required to mirror it unambiguously"
   531	            )
   532	        value = nodes[0]["value"]
   533	        if not isinstance(value, int) or isinstance(value, bool) or value <= 0:
   534	            _fail(f"rule {rule_id!r}'s '{fact} gte' bound is {value!r}, not a positive integer")
   535	        bounds.append(value)
   536	    return bounds[0], bounds[1]

   573	def build_support_rule(payload: dict[str, Any], row: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
   574	    """One ELIGIBILITY/SUPPORT rule, with its scope, covered purposes and
   575	    citations DERIVED from the product catalogue rather than transcribed."""
   576	    products = _products_by_code(payload)
   577	    code = row["product_code"]
   578	    if code not in products:
   579	        _fail(f"product {code!r} is not in the catalogue — cannot build {row['rule_id']!r}")
   580	    product = products[code]
   581	    purposes = list(row["purposes"])
   582	    unknown = [purpose for purpose in purposes if purpose not in (product.get("covered_purposes") or [])]
   583	    if unknown:
   584	        _fail(
   585	            f"{row['rule_id']!r} would cover {unknown} for {code}, which the product "
   586	            f"catalogue does not list among its covered_purposes "
   587	            f"({product.get('covered_purposes')})"
   588	        )
   589	    when = {
   590	        "op": "all",
   591	        "args": [
   592	            {"op": "intersects", "fact": "intent.purposes", "values": purposes},
   593	            *copy.deepcopy(row["premises"]),
   594	            {"op": "eq", "fact": row["qualifying_fact"], "value": True},
   595	        ],
   596	    }
   597	    return {
   598	        "when": when,
   599	        "scope": "PRODUCTS",
   600	        "stage": "ELIGIBILITY",
   601	        "effect": {
   602	            "type": "SUPPORT",
   603	            "reason_code": row["reason_code"],
   604	            "covered_purposes": purposes,
   605	        },
   606	        "rule_id": row["rule_id"],
   607	        "priority": 100,
   608	        "on_unknown": "NEEDS_INPUT",
   609	        "source_refs": list(product["source_refs"]),
   610	        "valid_period": {"to": None, "from": PACK_VALID_FROM},
   611	        "required_facts": _required_facts(when),
   612	        "explanation_key": f"explain.{row['rule_id']}",
   613	        "safety_critical": False,
   614	        "product_version_ids": [product["product_version_id"]],
   615	    }

   781	def fold(
   782	    seq20: dict[str, Any],
   783	    seq20_signed: dict[str, Any],
   784	    *,
   785	    observed_at: datetime | None = None,
   786	) -> dict[str, Any]:
   787	    """Return the seq-21 payload, or abort loudly.
   788	
   789	    ``seq20_signed`` is the signed seq-20 envelope and is REQUIRED, not
   790	    optional — see :func:`assert_anchor_is_a_verified_signed_artifact`.
   791	    ``observed_at`` is threaded into that signature check's clock so a test
   792	    pinning it is not left real-clock-dependent.
   793	    """
   794	    digest = hashlib.sha256(canonicalize_json(seq20)).hexdigest()
   795	    if digest != SEQ20_PAYLOAD_SHA256:
   796	        _fail(
   797	            "the seq-20 source is not the activated artifact: recomputed JCS "
   798	            f"digest {digest} != {SEQ20_PAYLOAD_SHA256}. Everything below would "
   799	            "otherwise be built on a payload production never ran."
   800	        )
   801	    assert_anchor_is_a_verified_signed_artifact(seq20_signed, digest, observed_at=observed_at)
   802	    if seq20.get("sequence") != 20:
   803	        _fail(f"expected sequence 20, got {seq20.get('sequence')!r}")
   804	
   805	    inherited_id = seq20.get("rule_pack_id")
   806	    expected_20_id = str(_rule_pack_id(20))
   807	    if inherited_id != expected_20_id:
   808	        _fail(
   809	            f"the seq-20 payload carries rule_pack_id={inherited_id!r}, but the "
   810	            f"uuid5 convention yields {expected_20_id!r} — the anchor is verified, "
   811	            "never assumed."
   812	        )
   813	    collisions = sorted(set(NEW_RULE_IDS) & set(_rules_by_id(seq20)))
   814	    if collisions:
   815	        _fail(f"rule(s) {collisions} already exist in seq-20 — this fold declares them as INSERTs")
   816	
   817	    _assert_target_products_have_no_eligibility_rule(seq20)
   818	    _assert_retired_review_rules_are_dormant(seq20)
   819	    _assert_employment_sponsor_scope_is_coherent(seq20)
   820	
   821	    new_rules = build_new_rules(seq20)
   822	
   823	    out = json.loads(json.dumps(seq20))
   824	    out["rules"] = [rule for rule in out["rules"] if rule["rule_id"] not in RETIRED_REVIEW_RULES]
   825	    out["rules"].extend(copy.deepcopy(rule) for rule in new_rules)
   826	
   827	    out["sequence"] = 21
   828	    out["rule_pack_id"] = str(_rule_pack_id(21))
   829	    out["version"] = FOLD_VERSION
   830	    out["created_at"] = FOLD_CREATED_AT
   831	    out["created_by"] = FOLD_CREATED_BY
   832	    out["valid_period"] = {"to": None, "from": PACK_VALID_FROM}
   833	    out["previous_payload_sha256"] = SEQ20_PAYLOAD_SHA256
   834	    out["rollback_of_payload_sha256"] = None
   835	
   836	    assert_only_expected_changes(seq20, out)
   837	    assert_changed_fields_hold_their_expected_values(out, expected_new_rules=new_rules)
   838	    RulePackPayload.model_validate(out)
   839	    return out
   840	
   890	    if signed_path == args.seq20_source or not signed_path.exists():
   891	        _fail(f"no signed seq-20 bundle at {signed_path} — pass --seq20-signed")
   892	
   893	    _assert_output_does_not_collide_with_inputs(
   894	        args.output,
   895	        {"--seq20-source": args.seq20_source, "--seq20-signed": signed_path},
   896	    )
   897	
   898	    seq20 = json.loads(args.seq20_source.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
   899	    seq20_signed = json.loads(signed_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
   900	    seq21 = fold(seq20, seq20_signed, observed_at=observed_at)
   901	    args.output.write_text(json.dumps(seq21, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
   902	    digest = hashlib.sha256(canonicalize_json(seq21)).hexdigest()
   903	    print(f"fold_pack_seq21: wrote {args.output}")
   904	    print(f"fold_pack_seq21: seq-21 payload_sha256 = {digest}")
   905	    print(f"fold_pack_seq21: retired {sorted(RETIRED_REVIEW_RULES)}")
   906	    print(f"fold_pack_seq21: inserted {sorted(NEW_RULE_IDS)}")
   907	    print("fold_pack_seq21: NOT SIGNED, NOT ACTIVATED — see sign_pack.py / activate_pack.py")
   908	    return 0

   340	def _safety_unknowns(entries: Sequence[_StageResult]) -> tuple[_StageResult, ...]:
   341	    """The subset of ``entries`` whose condition is UNKNOWN and whose rule
   342	    does not declare ``on_unknown=NO_EFFECT`` — i.e. an UNKNOWN result that
   343	    the rule author says *could* still change the outcome once resolved
   344	    (whether by asking the applicant, per ``NEEDS_INPUT``, or by escalating
   345	    to a human reviewer, per ``HUMAN_REVIEW`` — see
   346	    ``_partition_unknowns_by_policy`` for that split).
   347	    """
   348	    return tuple(
   349	        (rule, result)
   350	        for rule, result in entries
   351	        if result.truth is TruthValue.UNKNOWN and rule.on_unknown is not OnUnknownAction.NO_EFFECT
   352	    )
   353	
   354	
   355	def _partition_unknowns_by_policy(
   356	    entries: Sequence[_StageResult],
   357	) -> tuple[tuple[_StageResult, ...], tuple[_StageResult, ...]]:
   358	    """Split an already-``_safety_unknowns``-filtered sequence into
   359	    ``(review_unknowns, input_unknowns)`` by each rule's own ``on_unknown``
   360	    policy (gate round 1 item 4, 2026-07-19 — ``on_unknown=HUMAN_REVIEW`` was
   361	    previously a dead option, silently treated identically to
   362	    ``NEEDS_INPUT``).
   363	
   364	    A ``HUMAN_REVIEW``-tagged UNKNOWN contributes a review reason: the rule
   365	    author is saying "if we cannot determine this, put it in front of a
   366	    human — do not just ask the applicant for more facts". A
   367	    ``NEEDS_INPUT``-tagged UNKNOWN contributes a missing fact, exactly as
   368	    before.
   369	    """
   370	    review = tuple(
   371	        entry for entry in entries if entry[0].on_unknown is OnUnknownAction.HUMAN_REVIEW
   372	    )
   373	    needs_input = tuple(
   374	        entry for entry in entries if entry[0].on_unknown is OnUnknownAction.NEEDS_INPUT
   375	    )
   376	    return review, needs_input
   377
